## Update AI Config targeting

<a id="opIdpatchAIConfigTargeting"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://app.launchdarkly.com/api/v2/projects/string/ai-configs/string/targeting \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "instructions": [
      {
        "key": ""
      },
      {
        "key": ""
      }
    ],
    "comment": "comment",
    "environmentKey": "environmentKey"
  }'
```

`PATCH /api/v2/projects/{projectKey}/ai-configs/{configKey}/targeting`

Perform a partial update to an AI Config's targeting. The request body must be a valid semantic patch.

### Using semantic patches on an AI Config

To make a semantic patch request, you must append `domain-model=launchdarkly.semanticpatch` to your `Content-Type` header. To learn more, read [Updates using semantic patch](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/api#updates-using-semantic-patch).

The body of a semantic patch request for updating an AI Config's targeting takes the following properties:

* `comment` (string): (Optional) A description of the update.
* `environmentKey` (string): The key of the LaunchDarkly environment.
* `instructions` (array): (Required) A list of actions the update should perform. Each action in the list must be an object with a `kind` property that indicates the instruction. If the action requires parameters, you must include those parameters as additional fields in the object. The body of a single semantic patch can contain many different instructions.

### Instructions

Semantic patch requests support the following `kind` instructions for updating AI Configs.

<details>
<summary>Click to expand instructions for <strong>working with targeting and variations</strong> for AI Configs</summary>

#### addClauses

Adds the given clauses to the rule indicated by `ruleId`.

##### Parameters

- `ruleId`: ID of a rule in the AI Config.
- `clauses`: Array of clause objects, with `contextKind` (string), `attribute` (string), `op` (string), `negate` (boolean), and `values` (array of strings, numbers, or dates) properties. The `contextKind`, `attribute`, and `values` are case sensitive. The `op` must be lower-case.

Here's an example:

```json
{
  "environmentKey": "environment-key-123abc",
  "instructions": [{
    "kind": "addClauses",
    "ruleId": "a902ef4a-2faf-4eaf-88e1-ecc356708a29",
    "clauses": [{
      "contextKind": "user",
      "attribute": "country",
      "op": "in",
      "negate": false,
      "values": ["USA", "Canada"]
    }]
  }]
}
```

#### addRule

Adds a new targeting rule to the AI Config. The rule may contain `clauses` and serve the variation that `variationId` indicates, or serve a percentage rollout that `rolloutWeights`, `rolloutBucketBy`, and `rolloutContextKind` indicate.

If you set `beforeRuleId`, this adds the new rule before the indicated rule. Otherwise, adds the new rule to the end of the list.

##### Parameters

- `clauses`: Array of clause objects, with `contextKind` (string), `attribute` (string), `op` (string), `negate` (boolean), and `values` (array of strings, numbers, or dates) properties. The `contextKind`, `attribute`, and `values` are case sensitive. The `op` must be lower-case.
- `beforeRuleId`: (Optional) ID of a rule.
- Either
- `variationId`: ID of a variation.

or

- `rolloutWeights`: (Optional) Map of `variationId` to weight, in thousandths of a percent (0-100000).
- `rolloutBucketBy`: (Optional) Context attribute available in the specified `rolloutContextKind`.
- `rolloutContextKind`: (Optional) Context kind, defaults to `user`

Here's an example that uses a `variationId`:

```json
{
"environmentKey": "environment-key-123abc",
"instructions": [{
  "kind": "addRule",
  "variationId": "2f43f67c-3e4e-4945-a18a-26559378ca00",
  "clauses": [{
    "contextKind": "organization",
    "attribute": "located_in",
    "op": "in",
    "negate": false,
    "values": ["Sweden", "Norway"]
  }]
}]
}
```

Here's an example that uses a percentage rollout:

```json
{
"environmentKey": "environment-key-123abc",
"instructions": [{
  "kind": "addRule",
  "clauses": [{
    "contextKind": "organization",
    "attribute": "located_in",
    "op": "in",
    "negate": false,
    "values": ["Sweden", "Norway"]
  }],
  "rolloutContextKind": "organization",
  "rolloutWeights": {
    "2f43f67c-3e4e-4945-a18a-26559378ca00": 15000, // serve 15% this variation
    "e5830889-1ec5-4b0c-9cc9-c48790090c43": 85000  // serve 85% this variation
  }
}]
}
```

#### addTargets

Adds context keys to the individual context targets for the context kind that `contextKind` specifies and the variation that `variationId` specifies. Returns an error if this causes the AI Config to target the same context key in multiple variations.

##### Parameters

- `values`: List of context keys.
- `contextKind`: (Optional) Context kind to target, defaults to `user`
- `variationId`: ID of a variation.

Here's an example:

```json
{
"environmentKey": "environment-key-123abc",
"instructions": [{
  "kind": "addTargets",
  "values": ["context-key-123abc", "context-key-456def"],
  "variationId": "2f43f67c-3e4e-4945-a18a-26559378ca00"
}]
}
```

#### addValuesToClause

Adds `values` to the values of the clause that `ruleId` and `clauseId` indicate. Does not update the context kind, attribute, or operator.

##### Parameters

- `ruleId`: ID of a rule in the AI Config.
- `clauseId`: ID of a clause in that rule.
- `values`: Array of strings, case sensitive.

Here's an example:

```json
{
"environmentKey": "environment-key-123abc",
"instructions": [{
  "kind": "addValuesToClause",
  "ruleId": "a902ef4a-2faf-4eaf-88e1-ecc356708a29",
  "clauseId": "10a58772-3121-400f-846b-b8a04e8944ed",
  "values": ["beta_testers"]
}]
}
```

#### clearTargets

Removes all individual targets from the variation that `variationId` specifies. This includes both user and non-user targets.

##### Parameters

- `variationId`: ID of a variation.

Here's an example:

```json
{
"environmentKey": "environment-key-123abc",
"instructions": [ { "kind": "clearTargets", "variationId": "2f43f67c-3e4e-4945-a18a-26559378ca00" } ]
}
```

#### removeClauses

Removes the clauses specified by `clauseIds` from the rule indicated by `ruleId`.

##### Parameters

- `ruleId`: ID of a rule.
- `clauseIds`: Array of IDs of clauses in the rule.

Here's an example:

```json
{
"environmentKey": "environment-key-123abc",
"instructions": [{
  "kind": "removeClauses",
  "ruleId": "a902ef4a-2faf-4eaf-88e1-ecc356708a29",
  "clauseIds": ["10a58772-3121-400f-846b-b8a04e8944ed", "36a461dc-235e-4b08-97b9-73ce9365873e"]
}]
}
```

#### removeRule

Removes the targeting rule specified by `ruleId`. Does nothing if the rule does not exist.

##### Parameters

- `ruleId`: ID of a rule.

Here's an example:

```json
{
"environmentKey": "environment-key-123abc",
"instructions": [ { "kind": "removeRule", "ruleId": "a902ef4a-2faf-4eaf-88e1-ecc356708a29" } ]
}
```

#### removeTargets

Removes context keys from the individual context targets for the context kind that `contextKind` specifies and the variation that `variationId` specifies. Does nothing if the flag does not target the context keys.

##### Parameters

- `values`: List of context keys.
- `contextKind`: (Optional) Context kind to target, defaults to `user`
- `variationId`: ID of a variation.

Here's an example:

```json
{
"environmentKey": "environment-key-123abc",
"instructions": [{
  "kind": "removeTargets",
  "values": ["context-key-123abc", "context-key-456def"],
  "variationId": "2f43f67c-3e4e-4945-a18a-26559378ca00"
}]
}
```

#### removeValuesFromClause

Removes `values` from the values of the clause indicated by `ruleId` and `clauseId`. Does not update the context kind, attribute, or operator.

##### Parameters

- `ruleId`: ID of a rule.
- `clauseId`: ID of a clause in that rule.
- `values`: Array of strings, case sensitive.

Here's an example:

```json
{
"environmentKey": "environment-key-123abc",
"instructions": [{
  "kind": "removeValuesFromClause",
  "ruleId": "a902ef4a-2faf-4eaf-88e1-ecc356708a29",
  "clauseId": "10a58772-3121-400f-846b-b8a04e8944ed",
  "values": ["beta_testers"]
}]
}
```

#### reorderRules

Rearranges the rules to match the order given in `ruleIds`. Returns an error if `ruleIds` does not match the current set of rules on the AI Config.

##### Parameters

- `ruleIds`: Array of IDs of all rules.

Here's an example:

```json
{
"environmentKey": "environment-key-123abc",
"instructions": [{
  "kind": "reorderRules",
  "ruleIds": ["a902ef4a-2faf-4eaf-88e1-ecc356708a29", "63c238d1-835d-435e-8f21-c8d5e40b2a3d"]
}]
}
```

#### replaceRules

Removes all targeting rules for the AI Config and replaces them with the list you provide.

##### Parameters

- `rules`: A list of rules.

Here's an example:

```json
{
"environmentKey": "environment-key-123abc",
"instructions": [
  {
    "kind": "replaceRules",
    "rules": [
      {
        "variationId": "2f43f67c-3e4e-4945-a18a-26559378ca00",
        "description": "My new rule",
        "clauses": [
          {
            "contextKind": "user",
            "attribute": "segmentMatch",
            "op": "segmentMatch",
            "values": ["test"]
          }
        ]
      }
    ]
  }
]
}
```

#### replaceTargets

Removes all existing targeting and replaces it with the list of targets you provide.

##### Parameters

- `targets`: A list of context targeting. Each item in the list includes an optional `contextKind` that defaults to `user`, a required `variationId`, and a required list of `values`.

Here's an example:

```json
{
"environmentKey": "environment-key-123abc",
"instructions": [
  {
    "kind": "replaceTargets",
    "targets": [
      {
        "contextKind": "user",
        "variationId": "2f43f67c-3e4e-4945-a18a-26559378ca00",
        "values": ["user-key-123abc"]
      },
      {
        "contextKind": "device",
        "variationId": "e5830889-1ec5-4b0c-9cc9-c48790090c43",
        "values": ["device-key-456def"]
      }
    ]
  }
]
}
```

#### updateClause

Replaces the clause indicated by `ruleId` and `clauseId` with `clause`.

##### Parameters

- `ruleId`: ID of a rule.
- `clauseId`: ID of a clause in that rule.
- `clause`: New `clause` object, with `contextKind` (string), `attribute` (string), `op` (string), `negate` (boolean), and `values` (array of strings, numbers, or dates) properties. The `contextKind`, `attribute`, and `values` are case sensitive. The `op` must be lower-case.

Here's an example:

```json
{
"environmentKey": "environment-key-123abc",
"instructions": [{
  "kind": "updateClause",
  "ruleId": "a902ef4a-2faf-4eaf-88e1-ecc356708a29",
  "clauseId": "10c7462a-2062-45ba-a8bb-dfb3de0f8af5",
  "clause": {
    "contextKind": "user",
    "attribute": "country",
    "op": "in",
    "negate": false,
    "values": ["Mexico", "Canada"]
  }
}]
}
```

#### updateDefaultVariation

Updates the default on or off variation of the AI Config.

##### Parameters

- `onVariationValue`: (Optional) The value of the variation of the new on variation.
- `offVariationValue`: (Optional) The value of the variation of the new off variation

Here's an example:

```json
{
"instructions": [ { "kind": "updateDefaultVariation", "OnVariationValue": true, "OffVariationValue": false } ]
}
```

#### updateFallthroughVariationOrRollout

Updates the default or "fallthrough" rule for the AI Config, which the AI Config serves when a context matches none of the targeting rules. The rule can serve either the variation that `variationId` indicates, or a percentage rollout that `rolloutWeights` and `rolloutBucketBy` indicate.

##### Parameters

- `variationId`: ID of a variation.

or

- `rolloutWeights`: Map of `variationId` to weight, in thousandths of a percent (0-100000).
- `rolloutBucketBy`: (Optional) Context attribute available in the specified `rolloutContextKind`.
- `rolloutContextKind`: (Optional) Context kind, defaults to `user`

Here's an example that uses a `variationId`:

```json
{
"environmentKey": "environment-key-123abc",
"instructions": [{
  "kind": "updateFallthroughVariationOrRollout",
  "variationId": "2f43f67c-3e4e-4945-a18a-26559378ca00"
}]
}
```

Here's an example that uses a percentage rollout:

```json
{
"environmentKey": "environment-key-123abc",
"instructions": [{
  "kind": "updateFallthroughVariationOrRollout",
  "rolloutContextKind": "user",
  "rolloutWeights": {
    "2f43f67c-3e4e-4945-a18a-26559378ca00": 15000, // serve 15% this variation
    "e5830889-1ec5-4b0c-9cc9-c48790090c43": 85000  // serve 85% this variation
  }
}]
}
```

#### updateOffVariation

Updates the default off variation to `variationId`. The AI Config serves the default off variation when the AI Config's targeting is **Off**.

##### Parameters

- `variationId`: ID of a variation.

Here's an example:

```json
{
"environmentKey": "environment-key-123abc",
"instructions": [ { "kind": "updateOffVariation", "variationId": "2f43f67c-3e4e-4945-a18a-26559378ca00" } ]
}
```

#### updateRuleDescription

Updates the description of the targeting rule.

##### Parameters

- `description`: The new human-readable description for this rule.
- `ruleId`: The ID of the rule. You can retrieve this by making a GET request for the AI Config.

Here's an example:

```json
{
"environmentKey": "environment-key-123abc",
"instructions": [{
  "kind": "updateRuleDescription",
  "description": "New rule description",
  "ruleId": "a902ef4a-2faf-4eaf-88e1-ecc356708a29"
}]
}
```

#### updateRuleTrackEvents

Updates whether or not LaunchDarkly tracks events for the AI Config associated with this rule.

##### Parameters

- `ruleId`: The ID of the rule. You can retrieve this by making a GET request for the AI Config.
- `trackEvents`: Whether or not events are tracked.

Here's an example:

```json
{
"environmentKey": "environment-key-123abc",
"instructions": [{
  "kind": "updateRuleTrackEvents",
  "ruleId": "a902ef4a-2faf-4eaf-88e1-ecc356708a29",
  "trackEvents": true
}]
}
```

#### updateRuleVariationOrRollout

Updates what `ruleId` serves when its clauses evaluate to true. The rule can serve either the variation that `variationId` indicates, or a percent rollout that `rolloutWeights` and `rolloutBucketBy` indicate.

##### Parameters

- `ruleId`: ID of a rule.
- `variationId`: ID of a variation.

or

- `rolloutWeights`: Map of `variationId` to weight, in thousandths of a percent (0-100000).
- `rolloutBucketBy`: (Optional) Context attribute available in the specified `rolloutContextKind`.
- `rolloutContextKind`: (Optional) Context kind, defaults to `user`

Here's an example:

```json
{
"environmentKey": "environment-key-123abc",
"instructions": [{
  "kind": "updateRuleVariationOrRollout",
  "ruleId": "a902ef4a-2faf-4eaf-88e1-ecc356708a29",
  "variationId": "2f43f67c-3e4e-4945-a18a-26559378ca00"
}]
}
```

#### updateTrackEvents

Updates whether or not LaunchDarkly tracks events for the AI Config, for all rules.

##### Parameters

- `trackEvents`: Whether or not events are tracked.

Here's an example:

```json
{
"environmentKey": "environment-key-123abc",
"instructions": [ { "kind": "updateTrackEvents", "trackEvents": true } ]
}
```

#### updateTrackEventsFallthrough

Updates whether or not LaunchDarkly tracks events for the AI Config, for the default rule.

##### Parameters

- `trackEvents`: Whether or not events are tracked.

Here's an example:

```json
{
"environmentKey": "environment-key-123abc",
"instructions": [ { "kind": "updateTrackEventsFallthrough", "trackEvents": true } ]
}
```
</details>


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "instructions": [
    {
      "key": ""
    },
    {
      "key": ""
    }
  ],
  "comment": "comment",
  "environmentKey": "environmentKey"
}
```

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|AI Config targeting updated|[AIConfigTargeting](#schemaaiconfigtargeting)|
|400|Bad Request|Bad request|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|404|Not Found|Not found|[Error](#schemaerror)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
ApiKey
</aside>

## List AI Configs

<a id="opIdgetAIConfigs"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://app.launchdarkly.com/api/v2/projects/default/ai-configs \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /api/v2/projects/{projectKey}/ai-configs`

Get a list of all AI Configs in the given project.

<h3 id="list-ai-configs-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|projectKey|path|string|true|The project key|
|sort|query|string|false|A sort to apply to the list of AgentControl configs.|
|limit|query|integer|false|The number of resources to return.|
|offset|query|integer|false|Where to start in the list. Use this with pagination. For example, an offset of 10 skips the first ten items and then returns the next items in the list, up to the query `limit`.|
|filter|query|string|false|A filter to apply to the list.|

<h3 id="create-new-ai-config-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|projectKey|path|string|true|The project key|
|body|body|[AIConfigPost](#schemaaiconfigpost)|true|AI Config object to create|
|» description|body|string|false|A description of the AI Config|
|» key|body|string|true|A unique key for the AI Config|
|» maintainerId|body|string|false|The ID of the member who maintains this resource|
|» maintainerTeamKey|body|string|false|The key of the team that maintains this resource|
|» mode|body|string|false|The AI Config mode|
|» name|body|string|true|A human-readable name for the AI Config|
|» tags|body|[string]|false|Tags for this resource|
|» viewKeys|body|[string]|false|Keys of the views to add the AI Config to|
|» defaultVariation|body|[AIConfigVariationPost](#schemaaiconfigvariationpost)|false|none|
|» evaluationMetricKey|body|string|false|Evaluation metric key for this config|
|» isInverted|body|boolean|false|The success direction of a judge. Offline evaluations use it to decide whether a score passes.<br><br>- `true`: A lower score is better. Use this for a judge that scores bad output, such as a toxicity or hallucination judge.<br>- `false`: A higher score is better. Use this for a judge that scores good output, such as an accuracy or relevance judge.<br><br>**Required for a custom judge.** A custom judge has `mode` set to `judge` and a `key` that is not a built-in judge key. Built-in judge keys are `ld-ai-judge-accuracy`, `ld-ai-judge-relevance`, and `ld-ai-judge-toxicity`, with or without a `-<timestamp>` suffix such as `ld-ai-judge-accuracy-1760000000000`. For a built-in judge key, this field is optional, and the API always uses the built-in direction.<br><br>Do not send this field when `mode` is `agent` or `completion`.<br><br>This field is not in the schema's `required` list, because only custom judges need it.<br><br>The API returns a `400` error in these cases:<br>- `isInverted is required for a custom judge: ...`: You create a custom judge without this field. Send `true` or `false`.<br>- `isInverted is only supported for judge mode`: You send this field and `mode` is `agent` or `completion`. Remove the field, or set `mode` to `judge`.<br>- `isInverted is not supported`: Custom judges are not available for your account. Remove the field from the request.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» mode|agent|
|» mode|completion|
|» mode|judge|

## Update AI Config

<a id="opIdpatchAIConfig"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://app.launchdarkly.com/api/v2/projects/string/ai-configs/string \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "maintainerId": "507f1f77bcf86cd799439011",
    "maintainerTeamKey": "example-team-key",
    "name": "name",
    "description": "description",
    "evaluationMetricKey": "evaluationMetricKey",
    "defaultVariationKey": "defaultVariationKey",
    "isInverted": true,
    "tags": [
      "tags",
      "tags"
    ]
  }'
```

`PATCH /api/v2/projects/{projectKey}/ai-configs/{configKey}`

Edit an existing AI Config.

The request body must be a JSON object of the fields to update. The values you include replace the existing values for the fields.

Here's an example:
  ```
    {
      "description": "Example updated description",
      "tags": ["new-tag"]
    }
  ```


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "maintainerId": "507f1f77bcf86cd799439011",
  "maintainerTeamKey": "example-team-key",
  "name": "name",
  "description": "description",
  "evaluationMetricKey": "evaluationMetricKey",
  "defaultVariationKey": "defaultVariationKey",
  "isInverted": true,
  "tags": [
    "tags",
    "tags"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="update-ai-config-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|projectKey|path|string|true|The project key|
|configKey|path|string|true|The AI Config key|
|body|body|[AIConfigPatch](#schemaaiconfigpatch)|false|AI Config object to update|
|» defaultVariationKey|body|string|false|Key of the variation this config serves by default|
|» description|body|string|false|A description of the AI Config|
|» maintainerId|body|string|false|The ID of the member who maintains this resource|
|» maintainerTeamKey|body|string|false|The key of the team that maintains this resource|
|» name|body|string|false|A human-readable name for the AI Config|
|» tags|body|[string]|false|Tags for this resource|
|» evaluationMetricKey|body|string|false|Evaluation metric key for this config|
|» isInverted|body|boolean|false|The success direction of a judge. Offline evaluations use it to decide whether a score passes.<br><br>- `true`: A lower score is better. Use this for a judge that scores bad output, such as a toxicity or hallucination judge.<br>- `false`: A higher score is better. Use this for a judge that scores good output, such as an accuracy or relevance judge.<br><br>Send this field only when the AI Config's `mode` is `judge`. If you omit it, the current direction does not change. For a built-in judge key, the API always returns the built-in direction. Built-in judge keys are `ld-ai-judge-accuracy`, `ld-ai-judge-relevance`, and `ld-ai-judge-toxicity`, with or without a `-<timestamp>` suffix such as `ld-ai-judge-accuracy-1760000000000`.<br><br>The API returns a `400` error in these cases:<br>- `isInverted is only supported for judge mode`: You send this field and the AI Config's `mode` is `agent` or `completion`. Remove the field.<br>- `isInverted is not supported`: Custom judges are not available for your account. Remove the field from the request.<br>|

`POST /api/v2/projects/{projectKey}/ai-configs/{configKey}/variations`

Create a new variation for a given AI Config.

The <code>model</code> in the request body requires a <code>modelName</code> and <code>parameters</code>, for example:

```
  "model": {
    "modelName": "claude-3-opus-20240229",
    "parameters": {
      "max_tokens": 1024
    }
  }
```

<h3 id="create-ai-config-variation-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|projectKey|path|string|true|The project key|
|configKey|path|string|true|The AI Config key|
|body|body|[AIConfigVariationPost](#schemaaiconfigvariationpost)|true|AI Config variation object to create|
|» classifiers|body|[[Classifier](#schemaclassifier)]|false|Classifier rules for a judge variation. When this array is non-empty, messages must be empty.<br>|
|» comment|body|string|false|Human-readable description of this variation|
|» description|body|string|false|Returns the description for the agent. This is only returned for agent variations.|
|» instructions|body|string|false|Returns the instructions for the agent. This is only returned for agent variations.|
|» key|body|string|true|A unique key for the variation|
|» messages|body|[[Message](#schemamessage)]|false|The prompt messages for this variation|
|» model|body|object|false|Freeform JSON object. LaunchDarkly does not validate the keys. In a model config, `params` and `customParams` hold parameters that the provider's API accepts, for example `{"temperature": 0.7, "maxTokens": 4096}`.|
|» name|body|string|true|A human-readable name for the variation|
|» modelConfigKey|body|string|false|The key that GET /api/v2/projects/{projectKey}/ai-configs/model-configs returns for the<br>model config. Do not use a custom model config's ID, which is the provider model ID.<br>|
|» modelConfigVersion|body|integer|false|The exact model config version to set this variation to. Requires modelConfigKey to be<br>set, and the version must exist for that model config. When omitted, the variation<br>records the model config's current (latest) version.<br>|
|» outputFormat|body|object|false|JSON Schema defining the structured output format for the variation.|
|» tools|body|[[VariationToolPost](#schemavariationtoolpost)]|false|List of tools to use for this variation. The latest version of the tool will be used.|
|» toolKeys|body|[string]|false|List of tool keys to use for this variation. The latest version of the tool will be used.|
|» skills|body|[[VariationSkillPost](#schemavariationskillpost)]|false|List of agent skills to attach to this variation.|
|» judgeConfiguration|body|[JudgeConfiguration](#schemajudgeconfiguration)|false|none|

`PATCH /api/v2/projects/{projectKey}/ai-configs/{configKey}/variations/{variationKey}`

Edit an existing variation of an AI Config. This creates a new version of the variation.

The request body must be a JSON object of the fields to update. The values you include replace the existing values for the fields.

If the variation is in use in a project environment where approval settings require review for this AI Config, this endpoint returns 403 and the change must be submitted through an approval request.

Here's an example:
```
  {
    "messages": [
      {
        "role": "system",
        "content": "The new message"
      }
    ]
  }
```


> Body parameter

```json

  "judgeConfiguration": {
    "judges": [
      {
        "samplingRate": 0.36160767,
        "judgeConfigKey": "judgeConfigKey"
      },

        "judgeConfigKey": "judgeConfigKey"
      }
    ]
  },

  "tools": [
    {

    {

    }
  ],
  "skills": [

      "version": 1,
      "key": "key"
    },
    {
      "version": 1,
      "key": "key"
    }
  ],
  "toolKeys": [
    "toolKeys",
    "toolKeys"
  ],
  "classifiers": [
    {
      "instructions": "instructions",
      "criteria": "",
      "type": "bool",
      "key": "key"
    },
    {
      "instructions": "instructions",
      "criteria": "",
      "type": "bool",
      "key": "key"
    }
  ],
  "name": "name",

    {
      "role": "role",
      "content": "content"
    },
    {
      "role": "role",
      "content": "content"
    }
  ],
  "comment": "comment",
  "model": "{}",
  "state": "archived",
  "outputFormat": {
    "key": ""
  },
  "modelConfigVersion": 1
}
```

<h3 id="update-ai-config-variation-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|projectKey|path|string|true|The project key|
|configKey|path|string|true|The AI Config key|
|variationKey|path|string|true|The AI Config variation key|
|body|body|[AIConfigVariationPatch](#schemaaiconfigvariationpatch)|false|AI Config variation object to update|
|» classifiers|body|[[Classifier](#schemaclassifier)]|false|Replaces classifier rules on a judge variation. An empty array clears them. When this array is<br>non-empty, messages must be empty.<br>|
|» comment|body|string|false|Human-readable description of what this patch changes|
|» description|body|string|false|Description for agent when the config is in agent mode.|
|» instructions|body|string|false|Instructions for agent when the config is in agent mode.|
|» messages|body|[[Message](#schemamessage)]|false|The prompt messages for this variation|
|» model|body|object|false|Freeform JSON object. LaunchDarkly does not validate the keys. In a model config, `params` and `customParams` hold parameters that the provider's API accepts, for example `{"temperature": 0.7, "maxTokens": 4096}`.|
|» modelConfigKey|body|string|false|The key that GET /api/v2/projects/{projectKey}/ai-configs/model-configs returns for the<br>model config. Do not use a custom model config's ID, which is the provider model ID.<br>|
|» modelConfigVersion|body|integer|false|The exact model config version to set this variation to. Requires modelConfigKey to be<br>set (either in this patch or already on the variation), and the version must exist for<br>that model config. When omitted, the variation keeps the version it is currently set to,<br>unless the patch changes modelConfigKey, in which case the variation records the new<br>model config's current (latest) version.<br>|
|» name|body|string|false|A human-readable name for the variation|
|» outputFormat|body|object|false|JSON Schema defining the structured output format for the variation.|
|» published|body|boolean|false|Whether to publish this version of the variation|
|» state|body|string|false|The state to move the variation to. Omit this field to keep the current state.<br>- `archived`: Archive a published variation. You cannot archive a variation that is already archived. You also cannot archive the only variation of an AI Config. An AI Config itself cannot be archived.<br>- `published`: Restore an archived variation. You cannot publish a variation that is already published.<br>|
|» tools|body|[[VariationToolPost](#schemavariationtoolpost)]|false|List of tools to use for this variation. The latest version of the tool will be used.|
|» toolKeys|body|[string]|false|List of tool keys to use for this variation. The latest version of the tool will be used.|
|» skills|body|[[VariationSkillPost](#schemavariationskillpost)]|false|List of agent skills to attach to this variation. Replaces the current attachments.|
|» judgeConfiguration|body|[JudgeConfiguration](#schemajudgeconfiguration)|false|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» state|archived|
|» state|published|

## Create an AI model config

<a id="opIdpostModelConfig"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://app.launchdarkly.com/api/v2/projects/default/ai-configs/model-configs \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "costPerOutputToken": 0.00004,
    "costPerInputToken": 0.000005,
    "customParams": "{}",
    "maintainerTeamKey": "example-team-key",
    "icon": "openai",
    "params": "{}",
    "tags": [
      "image"
    ],
    "maintainerId": "507f1f77bcf86cd799439011",
    "provider": "OpenAI",
    "name": "GPT Image 2",
    "id": "gpt-image-2",
    "key": "OpenAI.gpt-image-2",
    "costPerCachedInputToken": 0.00000125
  }'
```

`POST /api/v2/projects/{projectKey}/ai-configs/model-configs`

Create an AI model config. You can use this in any variation for any config in your project.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "costPerOutputToken": 0.00004,
  "costPerInputToken": 0.000005,
  "customParams": "{}",
  "maintainerTeamKey": "example-team-key",
  "icon": "openai",
  "params": "{}",
  "tags": [
    "image"
  ],
  "maintainerId": "507f1f77bcf86cd799439011",
  "provider": "OpenAI",
  "name": "GPT Image 2",
  "id": "gpt-image-2",
  "key": "OpenAI.gpt-image-2",
  "costPerCachedInputToken": 0.00000125
}
```

<h3 id="create-an-ai-model-config-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|projectKey|path|string|true|The project key|
|body|body|[ModelConfigPost](#schemamodelconfigpost)|true|AI model config object to create|
|» name|body|string|true|Human readable name of the model|
|» key|body|string|true|Unique key for the model config in the project, in the format `Provider.model-id`. Config variations reject other formats. Keys of global catalog models are reserved.|
|» id|body|string|true|Model ID that the provider's API uses. Cannot be changed after creation.|
|» maintainerId|body|string|false|The member ID of the maintainer. Not applied on create. To set the maintainer, update the model config after you create it.|
|» maintainerTeamKey|body|string|false|The key of the team that maintains the model config. Not applied on create. To set the maintainer, update the model config after you create it.|
|» icon|body|string|false|Icon for the model|
|» provider|body|string|false|Provider for the model. Use the provider prefix of `key`. Cannot be changed after creation.|
|» params|body|object|false|Freeform JSON object. LaunchDarkly does not validate the keys. In a model config, `params` and `customParams` hold parameters that the provider's API accepts, for example `{"temperature": 0.7, "maxTokens": 4096}`.|
|» customParams|body|object|false|Freeform JSON object. LaunchDarkly does not validate the keys. In a model config, `params` and `customParams` hold parameters that the provider's API accepts, for example `{"temperature": 0.7, "maxTokens": 4096}`.|
|» tags|body|[string]|false|Tags for the model config|
|» costPerInputToken|body|number(double)|false|Cost per input token in USD|
|» costPerOutputToken|body|number(double)|false|Cost per output token in USD|
|» costPerCachedInputToken|body|number(double)|false|Cost per cached input token in USD|

<h3 id="update-an-ai-model-config-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|projectKey|path|string|true|The project key|
|modelConfigKey|path|string|true|The AI model config key|
|body|body|[ModelConfigPatch](#schemamodelconfigpatch)|true|AI model config object to update|
|» id|body|string|false|Immutable provider model identifier. To use a different model identifier, create a new model config.|
|» provider|body|string|false|Immutable model provider. To use a different provider, create a new model config.|
|» name|body|string|false|Human-readable name of the model|
|» costPerInputToken|body|number(double)|false|Cost per input token in USD|
|» costPerOutputToken|body|number(double)|false|Cost per output token in USD|
|» costPerCachedInputToken|body|number(double)|false|Cost per cached input token in USD|
|» params|body|object|false|Freeform JSON object. LaunchDarkly does not validate the keys. In a model config, `params` and `customParams` hold parameters that the provider's API accepts, for example `{"temperature": 0.7, "maxTokens": 4096}`.|
|» customParams|body|object|false|Freeform JSON object. LaunchDarkly does not validate the keys. In a model config, `params` and `customParams` hold parameters that the provider's API accepts, for example `{"temperature": 0.7, "maxTokens": 4096}`.|
|» tags|body|[string]|false|Tags for the model config. Replaces the current tags.|
|» maintainerId|body|string|false|The member ID of the new maintainer. Set `maintainerId` or `maintainerTeamKey`, not both. An empty string removes the maintainer.|
|» maintainerTeamKey|body|string|false|The key of the team to set as the new maintainer. Set `maintainerId` or `maintainerTeamKey`, not both.|

## List AI model config versions

|offset|query|integer|false|Where to start in the list. Use this with pagination. For example, an offset of 10 skips the first ten items and then returns the next items in the list, up to the query `limit`.|

```json
    "customParameters": {
      "requiresApproval": true,
      "timeoutMs": 5000
    },
    "key": "key",
```

```bash
  }'
```

## Create an agent skill

<a id="opIdpostAgentSkill"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://app.launchdarkly.com/api/v2/projects/string/ai-configs/skills \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "maintainerId": "507f1f77bcf86cd799439011",
    "name": "PDF extraction",
    "markdown": "markdown",
    "maintainerTeamKey": "example-team-key",
    "description": "Extracts text and tables from PDF files.",
    "key": "pdf-extraction",
    "tags": [
      "documents"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /api/v2/projects/{projectKey}/ai-configs/skills`

Create a new agent skill within the given project.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "maintainerId": "507f1f77bcf86cd799439011",
  "name": "PDF extraction",
  "markdown": "markdown",
  "maintainerTeamKey": "example-team-key",
  "description": "Extracts text and tables from PDF files.",
  "key": "pdf-extraction",
  "tags": [
    "documents"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-an-agent-skill-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|projectKey|path|string|true|The project key|
|body|body|[AgentSkillPost](#schemaagentskillpost)|true|Agent skill object to create|
|» key|body|string|true|A unique key for the agent skill. The key must match `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$`: it can only contain lowercase letters, numbers, or '-', and must start with a lowercase letter or number. The key can be at most 64 characters, and Windows reserved file names (`con`, `prn`, `aux`, `nul`, `com0`-`com9`, and `lpt0`-`lpt9`) aren't allowed.|
|» name|body|string|true|Human-readable name of the agent skill.|
|» description|body|string|false|Human-readable description of what the agent skill does.|
|» markdown|body|string|true|The verbatim SKILL.md content of the agent skill|
|» maintainerId|body|string|false|The ID of the member who maintains this resource|
|» maintainerTeamKey|body|string|false|The key of the team that maintains this resource|
|» tags|body|[string]|false|Tags for the agent skill. Tags can be used in custom role policies.|

`PATCH /api/v2/projects/{projectKey}/ai-configs/skills/{skillKey}`

Update an existing agent skill. Creates a new version of the skill.

```json
  "markdown": "markdown",

}
```

`POST /api/v2/projects/{projectKey}/agent-graphs`

Create a new agent graph within the given project.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "maintainerId": "507f1f77bcf86cd799439011",
  "rootConfigKey": "rootConfigKey",
  "name": "name",
  "maintainerTeamKey": "example-team-key",
  "edges": [
    {
      "sourceConfig": "sourceConfig",
      "targetConfig": "targetConfig",
      "handoff": "{}",
      "key": "key"
    },
    {
      "sourceConfig": "sourceConfig",
      "targetConfig": "targetConfig",
      "handoff": "{}",
      "key": "key"
    }
  ],
  "description": "description",
  "key": "key"
}
```

<h3 id="create-new-agent-graph-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|LD-API-Version|header|string|true|Version of the endpoint.|
|projectKey|path|string|true|The project key|
|body|body|[AgentGraphPost](#schemaagentgraphpost)|true|Agent graph object to create|
|» key|body|string|true|A unique key for the agent graph|
|» name|body|string|true|A human-readable name for the agent graph|
|» description|body|string|false|A description of the agent graph|
|» maintainerId|body|string|false|The ID of the member who maintains this agent graph|
|» maintainerTeamKey|body|string|false|The key of the team that maintains this agent graph|
|» rootConfigKey|body|string|false|The config key of the root node. A missing root implies a newly created graph with metadata only.|

```bash
curl https://app.launchdarkly.com/api/v2/projects/string/agent-graphs/string \
```

```bash
  -d '{

    "name": "name",
    "maintainerTeamKey": "example-team-key",
    "edges": [
      {
        "sourceConfig": "sourceConfig",
        "targetConfig": "targetConfig",
        "handoff": "{}",
        "key": "key"
      },
      {
        "sourceConfig": "sourceConfig",
        "targetConfig": "targetConfig",
        "handoff": "{}",
        "key": "key"
      }
    ],
    "description": "description"
  }'
```

`PATCH /api/v2/projects/{projectKey}/agent-graphs/{graphKey}`

Edit an existing agent graph.

The request body must be a JSON object of the fields to update. The values you include replace the existing values for the fields.

If the update includes `rootConfigKey` or `edges`, both must be present and will be treated as full replacements.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "maintainerId": "507f1f77bcf86cd799439011",
  "rootConfigKey": "rootConfigKey",
  "name": "name",
  "maintainerTeamKey": "example-team-key",
  "edges": [
    {
      "sourceConfig": "sourceConfig",
      "targetConfig": "targetConfig",
      "handoff": "{}",
      "key": "key"
    },
    {
      "sourceConfig": "sourceConfig",
      "targetConfig": "targetConfig",
      "handoff": "{}",
      "key": "key"
    }
  ],
  "description": "description"
}
```

<h3 id="update-agent-graph-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|LD-API-Version|header|string|true|Version of the endpoint.|
|projectKey|path|string|true|The project key|
|graphKey|path|string|true|The agent graph key|
|body|body|[AgentGraphPatch](#schemaagentgraphpatch)|false|Agent graph object to update|
|» name|body|string|false|A human-readable name for the agent graph|
|» description|body|string|false|A description of the agent graph|
|» maintainerId|body|string|false|The ID of the member who maintains this agent graph. Pass an empty string to remove maintainer.|
|» maintainerTeamKey|body|string|false|The key of the team that maintains this agent graph. Pass an empty string to remove maintainer.|
|» rootConfigKey|body|string|false|The config key of the root node. If present, edges must also be present.|
|» edges|body|[[AgentGraphEdge](#schemaagentgraphedge)]|false|The edges in the graph. If present, rootConfigKey must also be present. Replaces all existing edges.|

`GET /api/v2/projects/{projectKey}/agent-optimizations/{optimizationKey}/results`

Get the most recent result for each unique run of an agent optimization.

<h3 id="list-latest-agent-optimization-result-per-run-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|projectKey|path|string|true|The project key|
|optimizationKey|path|string|true|The agent optimization key|
|limit|query|integer|false|The number of resources to return.|
|offset|query|integer|false|Where to start in the list. Use this with pagination. For example, an offset of 10 skips the first ten items and then returns the next items in the list, up to the query `limit`.|

## Create agent optimization result

<a id="opIdpostAgentOptimizationResult"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://app.launchdarkly.com/api/v2/projects/string/agent-optimizations/string/results \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "instructions": "instructions",
    "agentOptimizationVersion": 0,
    "iteration": 6,
    "runId": "046b6c7f-0b8a-43b9-b35d-6489e6daee91",
    "userInput": "userInput",
    "parameters": {
      "key": ""
    }
  }'
```

`POST /api/v2/projects/{projectKey}/agent-optimizations/{optimizationKey}/results`

Create a new result for an agent optimization run.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "instructions": "instructions",
  "agentOptimizationVersion": 0,
  "iteration": 6,
  "runId": "046b6c7f-0b8a-43b9-b35d-6489e6daee91",
  "userInput": "userInput",
  "parameters": {
    "key": ""
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-agent-optimization-result-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|projectKey|path|string|true|The project key|
|optimizationKey|path|string|true|The agent optimization key|
|body|body|[AgentOptimizationResultPost](#schemaagentoptimizationresultpost)|true|Agent optimization result to create|
|» runId|body|string(uuid)|true|The ID of the run this result belongs to|
|» agentOptimizationVersion|body|integer|true|The version of the agent optimization used|
|» iteration|body|integer|true|The iteration number within the run|
|» instructions|body|string|true|The instructions used for this attempt|
|» userInput|body|string|true|The user input used for this attempt|
|» parameters|body|object|false|The model parameters used for this attempt|

## Delete an agent optimization run

> Code samples

```bash
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H 'LD-API-Version: beta'
```

`DELETE /api/v2/projects/{projectKey}/agent-optimizations/{optimizationKey}/runs/{runId}`

Delete all results for a specific run of an agent optimization. Returns a 404 if the optimization does not exist or if the run has no results. A run whose results have already been deleted is indistinguishable from a run that never existed, so repeating this request also returns a 404.

<h3 id="delete-an-agent-optimization-run-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|LD-API-Version|header|string|true|Version of the endpoint.|
|projectKey|path|string|true|The project key|
|optimizationKey|path|string|true|The agent optimization key|
|runId|path|string(uuid)|true|The agent optimization run ID|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|LD-API-Version|beta|

```json
  },
```

```json
  "createdVariationKey": "createdVariationKey"
}
```

<h3 id="update-an-agent-optimization-result-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|projectKey|path|string|true|The project key|
|optimizationKey|path|string|true|The agent optimization key|
|resultId|path|string(uuid)|true|The agent optimization result ID|
|body|body|[AgentOptimizationResultPatch](#schemaagentoptimizationresultpatch)|true|Agent optimization result fields to update|
|» status|body|[AgentOptimizationResultStatus](#schemaagentoptimizationresultstatus)|false|none|
|» activity|body|[AgentOptimizationResultActivity](#schemaagentoptimizationresultactivity)|false|none|
|» completionResponse|body|string|false|The model response|
|» variation|body|object|false|The variation that was tested|
|» scores|body|object|false|The scores for the response|
|» generationTokens|body|object|false|Token usage for generating the response|
|» evaluationTokens|body|object|false|Token usage for judging the response|
|» generationLatency|body|integer|false|How long the response took to generate|
|» evaluationLatencies|body|object|false|How long each evaluation took|
|» createdVariationKey|body|string|false|The key of the variation created from this result|

|» status|PASSED|

|» activity|PENDING|

|» activity|GENERATING_VARIATION|
|» activity|VALIDATING|
|» activity|COMPLETED|

<h1 id="launchdarkly-rest-api-announcements">Announcements</h1>

The announcements API lets you create and update a custom announcement banner that appears in the LaunchDarkly user interface for everyone in your organization. You can use the banner to display organization-wide information, such as upcoming holidays, code freeze periods, or reminders on best practices. You can have one banner visible at a time.

To learn more, read [Organization announcements](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/account/org-announcements).


## Get announcements

<a id="opIdgetAnnouncementsPublic"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://app.launchdarkly.com/api/v2/announcements \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /api/v2/announcements`

Get announcements

<h3 id="get-announcements-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|status|query|string|false|Filter announcements by status.|
|limit|query|integer|false|The number of announcements to return.|
|offset|query|integer|false|Where to start in the list. Use this with pagination. For example, an offset of 10 skips the first ten items and then returns the next items in the list, up to the query `limit`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|status|active|
|status|inactive|
|status|scheduled|

<h1 id="launchdarkly-rest-api-applications-beta">Applications (beta)</h1>

> ### This feature is in beta
>
> To use this feature, pass in a header including the `LD-API-Version` key with value set to `beta`. Use this header with each call. To learn more, read [Beta resources](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/api#beta-resources).
>
> Resources that are in beta are still undergoing testing and development. They may change without notice, including becoming backwards incompatible.

The applications API lets you create, update, delete, and search for applications and application versions.

Each application includes information about the app you're creating, and a set of versions of the app that you've released. You can use applications to target particular application versions in your feature flags more easily, and to handle unsupported application versions more gracefully.

In addition to creating applications through the applications API, you can also create applications in the LaunchDarkly user interface. To learn more, read [Applications and application versions](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/releases/applications). LaunchDarkly also creates applications and application versions automatically when a LaunchDarkly SDK evaluates a feature flag for a context that includes application information. To learn more, read [Automatic environment attributes](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/sdk/features/environment-attributes).

You can use an application in any project in your LaunchDarkly account.

### Filtering applications and application versions

The `filter` parameter supports the following operators: `equals`, `notEquals`, `anyOf`, `startsWith`.

You can also combine filters in the following ways:

- Use a comma (`,`) as an AND operator
- Use a vertical bar (`|`) as an OR operator
- Use parentheses (`()`) to group filters

#### Supported fields and operators

You can only filter certain fields in applications when using the `filter` parameter. Additionally, you can only filter some fields with certain operators.

When you search for applications, the `filter` parameter supports the following fields and operators:

|<div style="width:120px">Field</div> |Description |Supported operators |
|---|---|---|
|`key` | The application or application version key, a unique identifier |`equals`, `notEquals`, `anyOf` |
|`name` | The application name or application version name |`equals`, `notEquals`, `anyOf`, `startsWith` |
|`autoAdded` | Whether the application or application version was automatically created because it was included in a context when a LaunchDarkly SDK evaluated a feature flag, or was created through the LaunchDarkly UI or REST API |`equals`, `notEquals` |
|`kind` | The application kind, one of `mobile`, `server`, `browser`. Only available for [Get applications](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/api/applications-beta/get-applications). |`equals`, `notEquals`, `anyOf` |
|`supported` | Whether a mobile application version is supported or unsupported. Only available for [Get application versions by application key](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/api/applications-beta/get-application-versions).|`equals`, `notEquals` |

For example, the filter `?filter=kind anyOf ["mobile", "server"]` matches applications whose `kind` is either `mobile` or `server`. The filter is not case-sensitive.

The documented values for `filter` query parameters are prior to URL encoding. For example, the `[` in `?filter=kind anyOf ["mobile", "server"]` must be encoded to `%5B`.

### Sorting applications and application versions

LaunchDarkly supports the following fields for sorting:
- `name` sorts by application name.
- `creationDate` sorts by the creation date of the application.

By default, the sort is in ascending order. Use `-` to sort in descending order. For example, `?sort=name` sorts the response by application name in ascending order, and `?sort=-name` sorts in descending order.


## Get applications

<a id="opIdgetApplications"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://app.launchdarkly.com/api/v2/applications \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /api/v2/applications`


Get a list of applications.

### Expanding the applications response

LaunchDarkly supports expanding the "Get applications" response to include additional fields.

To expand the response, append the `expand` query parameter and include the following:

* `flags` includes details on the flags that have been evaluated by the application

For example, use `?expand=flags` to include the `flags` field in the response. By default, this field is **not** included in the response.


<h3 id="get-applications-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|filter|query|string(string)|false|Accepts filter by `key`, `name`, `kind`, and `autoAdded`. To learn more about the filter syntax, read [Filtering applications and application versions](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/api/applications-beta#filtering-applications-and-application-versions).|
|limit|query|integer(int64)|false|The number of applications to return. Defaults to 10.|
|offset|query|integer(int64)|false|Where to start in the list. Use this with pagination. For example, an offset of 10 skips the first ten items and then returns the next items in the list, up to the query `limit`.|
|sort|query|string(string)|false|Accepts sorting order and fields. Fields can be comma separated. Possible fields are `creationDate`, `name`. Examples: `sort=name` sort by names ascending, `sort=-name,creationDate` sort by names descending and creationDate ascending.|
|expand|query|string(string)|false|A comma-separated list of properties that can reveal additional information in the response. Options: `flags`.|

<h1 id="launchdarkly-rest-api-approvals">Approvals</h1>

An account member can request approval on changes to a flag or AgentControl config's targeting or variations, or to a segment's targeting. Members may be required to request approval depending on the settings in their LaunchDarkly project. Members can optionally request an approval even if it is not required.

An approval request prevents a change from being applied without approval from another member. Select up to ten members as reviewers. Reviewers receive an email notification, but anyone with sufficient permissions can review a pending approval request. A change needs at least one approval before you can apply it. To learn more, read [Approvals](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/releases/approvals).

Changes that conflict will fail if approved and applied, and the flag or segment will not be updated.

Several of the endpoints in the approvals API require an approval request ID. The approval request ID is returned as part of the [Create approval request](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/api/approvals/post-approval-request) and [List approval requests for a flag](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/api/approvals/get-approvals-for-flag) responses. It is the `_id` field, or the `_id` field of each element in the `items` array. If you created the approval request as part of a [workflow](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/api/workflows), you can also use a workflow ID as the approval request ID. The workflow ID is returned as part of the [Create workflow](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/api/workflows/post-workflow) and [Get workflows](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/api/workflows/get-workflows) responses. It is the `_id` field, or the `_id` field of each element in the `items` array.


## List approval requests

<a id="opIdgetApprovalRequests"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://app.launchdarkly.com/api/v2/approval-requests \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /api/v2/approval-requests`

Get all approval requests.

### Filtering approvals

LaunchDarkly supports the `filter` query param for filtering, with the following fields:

- `notifyMemberIds` filters for only approvals that are assigned to a member in the specified list. For example: `filter=notifyMemberIds anyOf ["memberId1", "memberId2"]`.
- `requestorId` filters for only approvals that correspond to the ID of the member who requested the approval. For example: `filter=requestorId equals 457034721476302714390214`.
- `resourceId` filters for only approvals that correspond to the the specified resource identifier. For example: `filter=resourceId equals proj/my-project:env/my-environment:flag/my-flag`.
- `resourceKind` filters for only approvals that correspond to the specified resource kind. For example: `filter=resourceKind equals flag`. Currently, `flag`, `segment`, and `aiConfig` resource kinds are supported.
- `reviewStatus` filters for only approvals which correspond to the review status in the specified list. The possible values are `approved`, `declined`, and `pending`. For example: `filter=reviewStatus anyOf ["pending", "approved"]`.
- `status` filters for only approvals which correspond to the status in the specified list. The possible values are `pending`, `scheduled`, `failed`, and `completed`. For example: `filter=status anyOf ["pending", "scheduled"]`.

You can also apply multiple filters at once. For example, setting `filter=projectKey equals my-project, reviewStatus anyOf ["pending","approved"]` matches approval requests which correspond to the `my-project` project key, and a review status of either `pending` or `approved`.

### Expanding approval response

LaunchDarkly supports the `expand` query param to include additional fields in the response, with the following fields:

- `flag` includes the flag the approval request belongs to
- `project` includes the project the approval request belongs to
- `environments` includes the environments the approval request relates to

For example, `expand=project,flag` includes the `project` and `flag` fields in the response.


<h3 id="list-approval-requests-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|filter|query|string(string)|false|A comma-separated list of filters. Each filter is of the form `field operator value`. Supported fields are explained above.|
|expand|query|string(string)|false|A comma-separated list of fields to expand in the response. Supported fields are explained above.|
|limit|query|integer(int64)|false|The number of approvals to return. Defaults to 20. Maximum limit is 200.|
|offset|query|integer(int64)|false|Where to start in the list. Use this with pagination. For example, an offset of 10 skips the first ten items and then returns the next items in the list, up to the query `limit`.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "items": [
    {
      "_id": "12ab3c45de678910abc12345",
      "_version": 1,
      "creationDate": "1654104600000",
      "serviceKind": "launchdarkly",
      "requestorId": "12ab3c45de678910abc12345",
      "description": "example: request approval from someone",
      "reviewStatus": "pending",
      "allReviews": [
        {
          "_id": "12ab3c45de678910abc12345",
          "kind": "approve",
          "creationDate": "1653606981113",
          "comment": "Approved!",
          "memberId": "12ab3c45de678910abc12345",
          "serviceTokenId": "12ab3c45de678910abc12345"
        }
      ],
      "notifyMemberIds": [
        "1234a56b7c89d012345e678f"
      ],
      "notifyTeamKeys": [
        "example-reviewer-team"
      ],
      "appliedDate": "1654104600000",
      "appliedByMemberId": "1234a56b7c89d012345e678f",
      "appliedByServiceTokenId": "1234a56b7c89d012345e678f",
      "status": "pending",
      "instructions": "[{\"kind\": \"turnFlagOn\"}]",
      "conflicts": [
        {
          "instruction": {
            "property1": null,
            "property2": null
```

## Create approval request

<a id="opIdpostApprovalRequest"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://app.launchdarkly.com/api/v2/approval-requests \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "resourceId": "proj/projKey:env/envKey:flag/flagKey",
    "comment": "optional comment",
    "description": "Requesting to update targeting",
    "instructions": "[{\"kind\": \"addUserTargets\", \"values\": [ \"user-key-123abc\"], \"variationId\": \"ce67d625-a8b9-4fb5-a344-ab909d9d4f4d\" }]",
    "notifyMemberIds": [
      "1234a56b7c89d012345e678f"
    ],
    "notifyTeamKeys": [
      "example-reviewer-team"
    ],
    "integrationConfig": {
      "property1": null,
      "property2": null
    }
  }'
```

`POST /api/v2/approval-requests`

Create an approval request.

This endpoint requires a list of `instructions`, in semantic patch format, that will be applied when the approval request is approved and applied.

### Flags

If you are creating an approval request for a flag, you can use the following `instructions`:

- `addVariation`
- `removeVariation`
- `updateVariation`
- `updateDefaultVariation`

For details on using these instructions, read [Update feature flag](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/api/feature-flags/patch-feature-flag).

To create an approval for a flag specific to an environment, use [Create approval request for a flag](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/api/approvals/post-approval-request-for-flag).

### AgentControl

If you are creating an approval request for an AgentControl config, you can use the semantic patch instructions listed under [Update config targeting](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/api/agent-control/patch-ai-config-targeting).

### Segments

If you are creating an approval request for a segment, you can use the semantic patch instructions listed under [Patch segment](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/api/segments/patch-segment).


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "resourceId": "proj/projKey:env/envKey:flag/flagKey",
  "comment": "optional comment",
  "description": "Requesting to update targeting",
  "instructions": "[{\"kind\": \"addUserTargets\", \"values\": [ \"user-key-123abc\"], \"variationId\": \"ce67d625-a8b9-4fb5-a344-ab909d9d4f4d\" }]",
  "notifyMemberIds": [
    "1234a56b7c89d012345e678f"
  ],
  "notifyTeamKeys": [
    "example-reviewer-team"
  ],
  "integrationConfig": {
    "property1": null,
    "property2": null
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-approval-request-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[CreateApprovalRequestRequest](#schemacreateapprovalrequestrequest)|true|none|
|» resourceId|body|string|true|String representation of the resource specifier|
|» comment|body|string|false|Optional comment describing the approval request|
|» description|body|string|true|A brief description of the changes you're requesting|
|» instructions|body|[Instructions](#schemainstructions)|true|List of instructions in semantic patch format to be applied to the feature flag. Review the [Update feature flag](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/ld-docs/api/feature-flags/patch-feature-flag) documentation for details on available instructions.|
|» notifyMemberIds|body|[string]|false|An array of member IDs. These members are notified to review the approval request.|
|» notifyTeamKeys|body|[string]|false|An array of team keys. The members of these teams are notified to review the approval request.|
|» integrationConfig|body|[FormVariableConfig](#schemaformvariableconfig)|false|Additional approval request fields for third-party integration approval systems. If you are using a third-party integration to manage approval requests, these additional fields will be described in the <code>manifest.json</code> for that integration, at https://github.com/launchdarkly/integration-framework.|

## Get approval request

<a id="opIdgetApprovalRequest"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://app.launchdarkly.com/api/v2/approval-requests/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /api/v2/approval-requests/{id}`

Get an approval request by approval request ID.

### Expanding approval response

LaunchDarkly supports the `expand` query param to include additional fields in the response, with the following fields:

- `environments` includes the environments the approval request relates to
- `flag` includes the flag the approval request belongs to
- `project` includes the project the approval request belongs to
- `resource` includes details on the resource (flag or segment) the approval request relates to

For example, `expand=project,flag` includes the `project` and `flag` fields in the response.


<h3 id="get-approval-request-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string(string)|true|The approval request ID|
|expand|query|string(string)|false|A comma-separated list of fields to expand in the response. Supported fields are explained above.|

## Apply approval request

<a id="opIdpostApprovalRequestApply"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://app.launchdarkly.com/api/v2/approval-requests/string/apply \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "comment": "Looks good, thanks for updating"
  }'
```

`POST /api/v2/approval-requests/{id}/apply`

Apply an approval request that has been approved. This endpoint works with any approval requests.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "comment": "Looks good, thanks for updating"
}
```

<h3 id="apply-approval-request-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string(string)|true|The approval request ID|
|body|body|[postApprovalRequestApplyRequest](#schemapostapprovalrequestapplyrequest)|true|none|
|» comment|body|string|false|Optional comment about the approval request|

## Update approval request

<a id="opIdpatchApprovalRequest"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://app.launchdarkly.com/api/v2/approval-requests/string \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "instructions": [
      {
        "kind": "updateDescription",
        "value": "New description"
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`PATCH /api/v2/approval-requests/{id}`

Perform a partial update to an approval request. Updating an approval request uses the semantic patch format. This endpoint works with any approval requests.

To make a semantic patch request, you must append `domain-model=launchdarkly.semanticpatch` to your `Content-Type` header. To learn more, read [Updates using semantic patch](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/api#updates-using-semantic-patch).

### Instructions

Semantic patch requests support the following `kind` instructions for updating an approval request.

#### addReviewers

Adds the specified members and teams to the existing list of reviewers. You must include at least one of `notifyMemberIds` and `notifyTeamKeys`.

##### Parameters

- `notifyMemberIds`: (Optional) List of member IDs.
- `notifyTeamKeys`: (Optional) List of team keys.

Here's an example:

```json
{
  "instructions": [{
    "kind": "addReviewers",
    "notifyMemberIds": [ "user-key-123abc", "user-key-456def" ],
    "notifyTeamKeys": [ "team-key-789abc"]
  }]
}
```

#### updateDescription

Updates the description (title) of the approval request.

##### Parameters

- `value`: (Required) The new description for the approval request. Must be non-empty and no more than 5000 characters.

Here's an example:

```json
{
  "instructions": [{
    "kind": "updateDescription",
    "value": "Updated approval request title"
  }]
}
```


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "instructions": [
    {
      "kind": "updateDescription",
      "value": "New description"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="update-approval-request-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string(string)|true|The approval ID|
|body|body|[approvalRequestPatchInput](#schemaapprovalrequestpatchinput)|true|none|
|» comment|body|string|false|Optional comment describing the update|
|» instructions|body|[Instructions](#schemainstructions)|true|The instructions to perform when updating|

<a id="opIdpatchApprovalRequestSettings"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://app.launchdarkly.com/api/v2/approval-requests/projects/default/settings \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H 'LD-API-Version: beta' \
  -d '{
    "resourceKind": "resourceKind",
    "serviceKind": "launchdarkly",
    "canReviewOwnRequest": false,
    "requiredApprovalTags": [
      "require-approval"
    ],
    "serviceConfig": {},
    "serviceKindConfigurationId": "1ef45a85-218f-4428-a8b2-a97e5f56c258",
    "bypassApprovalsForPendingChanges": false,
    "canApplyDeclinedChanges": true,
    "minNumApprovals": 1,
    "autoApplyApprovedChanges": true,
    "required": true,
    "environmentKey": "environmentKey"
  }'
```

`PATCH /api/v2/approval-requests/projects/{projectKey}/settings`

Perform a partial update to approval request settings

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "resourceKind": "resourceKind",
  "serviceKind": "launchdarkly",
  "canReviewOwnRequest": false,
  "requiredApprovalTags": [
    "require-approval"
  ],
  "serviceConfig": {},
  "serviceKindConfigurationId": "1ef45a85-218f-4428-a8b2-a97e5f56c258",
  "bypassApprovalsForPendingChanges": false,
  "canApplyDeclinedChanges": true,
  "minNumApprovals": 1,
  "autoApplyApprovedChanges": true,
  "required": true,
  "environmentKey": "environmentKey"
}
```

<h3 id="update-approval-request-settings-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|LD-API-Version|header|string|true|Version of the endpoint.|
|projectKey|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|[ApprovalRequestSettingsPatch](#schemaapprovalrequestsettingspatch)|false|Approval request settings to update|
|» autoApplyApprovedChanges|body|boolean \| null|false|Automatically apply changes that have been approved by all reviewers. This field is only applicable for approval services other than LaunchDarkly.<br>|
|» bypassApprovalsForPendingChanges|body|boolean|false|Whether to skip approvals for pending changes|
|» canApplyDeclinedChanges|body|boolean|false|Allow applying the change as long as at least one person has approved|
|» canReviewOwnRequest|body|boolean|false|Allow someone who makes an approval request to apply their own change|
|» environmentKey|body|string|true|none|
|» minNumApprovals|body|integer(int)|false|Sets the amount of approvals required before a member can apply a change. The minimum is one and the maximum is five.<br>|
|» required|body|boolean|false|If approvals are required for this environment|
|» requiredApprovalTags|body|[string]|false|Require approval only on flags with the provided tags. Otherwise all flags will require approval.<br>|
|» resourceKind|body|string|true|none|
|» serviceConfig|body|object|false|Arbitrary service-specific configuration|
|» serviceKind|body|string|false|Which service to use for managing approvals|
|» serviceKindConfigurationId|body|string \| null|false|Optional integration configuration ID of a custom approval integration. This is an Enterprise-only feature.<br>|

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|

<h1 id="launchdarkly-rest-api-audit-log">Audit log</h1>

LaunchDarkly maintains a record of all the changes made to any resource in the system. You can access this history using the audit log API, including filtering by timestamps, or using a custom policy to select which entries to receive.

Several of the endpoints in the audit log API require an audit log entry ID. The audit log entry ID is returned as part of the [List audit log entries](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/api/audit-log/get-audit-log-entries) response. It is the `_id` field of each element in the `items` array.

In the LaunchDarkly UI, this information appears on the **Change history** page. To learn more, read [Change history](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/observability/change-history).


## List audit log entries

<a id="opIdgetAuditLogEntries"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://app.launchdarkly.com/api/v2/auditlog \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /api/v2/auditlog`

Get a list of all audit log entries. The query parameters let you restrict the results that return by date ranges, resource specifiers, or a full-text search query.

LaunchDarkly uses a resource specifier syntax to name resources or collections of resources. To learn more, read [Specifying resources in the advanced editor](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/account/roles/role-resources#specifying-resources-in-the-advanced-editor).


<h3 id="list-audit-log-entries-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|before|query|integer(int64)|false|A timestamp filter, expressed as a Unix epoch time in milliseconds.  All entries this returns occurred before the timestamp.|
|after|query|integer(int64)|false|A timestamp filter, expressed as a Unix epoch time in milliseconds. All entries this returns occurred after the timestamp.|
|q|query|string(string)|false|Text to search for. You can search for the full or partial name of the resource.|
|limit|query|integer(int64)|false|A limit on the number of audit log entries that return. Set between 1 and 20. The default is 10.|
|spec|query|string(string)|false|A resource specifier that lets you filter audit log listings by resource|
|member|query|string(string)|false|A member ID that lets you filter audit log listings by the member who made the change. Repeat the parameter to filter by multiple members.|
|token|query|string(string)|false|An access token ID that lets you filter audit log listings by the token that made the change. Repeat the parameter to filter by multiple tokens.|

## Search audit log entries

<a id="opIdpostAuditLogEntries"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://app.launchdarkly.com/api/v2/auditlog \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '[
    {
      "resources": [
        "proj/*:env/*:flag/*;testing-tag"
      ],
      "notResources": [
        "string"
      ],
      "actions": [
        "*"
      ],
      "notActions": [
        "string"
      ],
      "effect": "allow"
    }
  ]'
```

`POST /api/v2/auditlog`

Search your audit log entries. The query parameters let you restrict the results that return by date ranges, or a full-text search query. The request body lets you restrict the results that return by resource specifiers.

LaunchDarkly uses a resource specifier syntax to name resources or collections of resources. To learn more, read [Specifying resources in the advanced editor](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/account/roles/role-resources#specifying-resources-in-the-advanced-editor).


> Body parameter

```json
[
  {
    "resources": [
      "proj/*:env/*:flag/*;testing-tag"
    ],
    "notResources": [
      "string"
    ],
    "actions": [
      "*"
    ],
    "notActions": [
      "string"
    ],
    "effect": "allow"
  }
]
```

<h3 id="search-audit-log-entries-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|before|query|integer(int64)|false|A timestamp filter, expressed as a Unix epoch time in milliseconds.  All entries returned occurred before the timestamp.|
|after|query|integer(int64)|false|A timestamp filter, expressed as a Unix epoch time in milliseconds. All entries returned occurred after the timestamp.|
|q|query|string(string)|false|Text to search for. You can search for the full or partial name of the resource.|
|limit|query|integer(int64)|false|A limit on the number of audit log entries that return. Set between 1 and 20. The default is 10.|
|member|query|string(string)|false|A member ID that lets you filter audit log listings by the member who made the change. Repeat the parameter to filter by multiple members.|
|token|query|string(string)|false|An access token ID that lets you filter audit log listings by the token that made the change. Repeat the parameter to filter by multiple tokens.|
|body|body|[StatementPostList](#schemastatementpostlist)|false|none|

## Get audit log entry counts

<a id="opIdpostAuditLogEntryCounts"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://app.launchdarkly.com/api/v2/auditlog/counts?after=0' \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '[
    {
      "resources": [
        "proj/*:env/*:flag/*;testing-tag"
      ],
      "notResources": [
        "string"
      ],
      "actions": [
        "*"
      ],
      "notActions": [
        "string"
      ],
      "effect": "allow"
    }
  ]'
```

`POST /api/v2/auditlog/counts`

Returns aggregate counts of audit log entries per time bucket. Used for dashboard overlays that show flag targeting changes.

> Body parameter

```json
[
  {
    "resources": [
      "proj/*:env/*:flag/*;testing-tag"
    ],
    "notResources": [
      "string"
    ],
    "actions": [
      "*"
    ],
    "notActions": [
      "string"
    ],
    "effect": "allow"
  }
]
```

<h3 id="get-audit-log-entry-counts-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|before|query|integer(int64)|false|A timestamp filter, expressed as a Unix epoch time in milliseconds. Defaults to now.|
|after|query|integer(int64)|true|A timestamp filter, expressed as a Unix epoch time in milliseconds. Required.|
|buckets|query|integer(int64)|false|Number of time buckets to divide the range into. Default 50, max 500.|
|member|query|string(string)|false|A member ID that lets you filter counts to changes made by that member. Repeat the parameter to filter by multiple members.|
|token|query|string(string)|false|An access token ID that lets you filter counts to changes made by that token. Repeat the parameter to filter by multiple tokens.|
|body|body|[StatementPostList](#schemastatementpostlist)|true|none|

## Get audit log entry

<a id="opIdgetAuditLogEntry"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://app.launchdarkly.com/api/v2/auditlog/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /api/v2/auditlog/{id}`

Fetch a detailed audit log entry representation. The detailed representation includes several fields that are not present in the summary representation, including:

- `previousVersion`: a JSON representation of the previous version of the entity.
- `currentVersion`: a JSON representation of the current version of the entity.
- `delta`: the JSON patch body that was used in the request to update the entity. This is only included if the update was made through a [JSON patch](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/api#updates-using-json-patch). It is null when the update was made using [semantic patch](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/api#updates-using-semantic-patch). Because most [flag updates](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/api/feature-flags/patch-feature-flag) are made using semantic patch, this field is rarely returned.


<h3 id="get-audit-log-entry-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string(string)|true|The ID of the audit log entry|
