## Update team

<a id="opIdpatchTeam"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://app.launchdarkly.com/api/v2/teams/string \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "comment": "Optional comment about the update",
    "instructions": [
      {
        "kind": "updateDescription",
        "value": "New description for the team"
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`PATCH /api/v2/teams/{teamKey}`

Perform a partial update to a team. Updating a team uses the semantic patch format.

To make a semantic patch request, you must append `domain-model=launchdarkly.semanticpatch` to your `Content-Type` header. To learn more, read [Updates using semantic patch](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/api#updates-using-semantic-patch).

### Instructions

Semantic patch requests support the following `kind` instructions for updating teams. Several of the instructions require one or more member IDs as parameters. The member ID is returned as part of the [List account members](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/api/account-members/get-members) response. It is the `_id` field of each element in the `items` array.


<details>
<summary>Click to expand instructions for <strong>updating teams</strong></summary>

#### addCustomRoles

Adds custom roles to the team. Team members will have these custom roles granted to them.

##### Parameters

- `values`: List of custom role keys.

Here's an example:

```json
{
  "instructions": [{
    "kind": "addCustomRoles",
    "values": [ "example-custom-role" ]
  }]
}
```

#### addMembers

Adds members to the team.

##### Parameters

- `values`: List of member IDs to add.

Here's an example:

```json
{
  "instructions": [{
    "kind": "addMembers",
    "values": [ "1234a56b7c89d012345e678f", "507f1f77bcf86cd799439011" ]
  }]
}
```

#### addPermissionGrants

Adds permission grants to members for the team. For example, a permission grant could allow a member to act as a team maintainer. A permission grant may have either an `actionSet` or a list of `actions` but not both at the same time. The members do not have to be team members to have a permission grant for the team.

##### Parameters

- `actionSet`: Name of the action set.
- `actions`: List of actions.
- `memberIDs`: List of member IDs.

Here's an example:

```json
{
  "instructions": [{
    "kind": "addPermissionGrants",
    "actions": [ "updateTeamName", "updateTeamDescription" ],
    "memberIDs": [ "1234a56b7c89d012345e678f", "507f1f77bcf86cd799439011" ]
  }]
}
```

#### addRoleAttribute

Adds a role attribute to a team. Team members will have these role attribute values scoped for all custom roles granted to them.

##### Parameters

- `key`: The role attribute key to add.
- `values`: List of role attribute values for that key.

Here's an example:

```json
{
  "instructions": [
    {
      "kind": "addRoleAttribute",
      "key": "testAttribute",
      "values": ["someNewValue", "someOtherNewValue"]
    }
  ]
}
```

#### removeCustomRoles

Removes custom roles from the team. The app will no longer grant these custom roles to the team members.

##### Parameters

- `values`: List of custom role keys.

Here's an example:

```json
{
  "instructions": [{
    "kind": "removeCustomRoles",
    "values": [ "example-custom-role" ]
  }]
}
```

#### removeMembers

Removes members from the team.

##### Parameters

- `values`: List of member IDs to remove.

Here's an example:

```json
{
  "instructions": [{
    "kind": "removeMembers",
    "values": [ "1234a56b7c89d012345e678f", "507f1f77bcf86cd799439011" ]
  }]
}
```

#### removePermissionGrants

Removes permission grants from members for the team. A permission grant may have either an `actionSet` or a list of `actions` but not both at the same time. The `actionSet` and `actions` must match an existing permission grant.

##### Parameters

- `actionSet`: Name of the action set.
- `actions`: List of actions.
- `memberIDs`: List of member IDs.

Here's an example:

```json
{
  "instructions": [{
    "kind": "removePermissionGrants",
    "actions": [ "updateTeamName", "updateTeamDescription" ],
    "memberIDs": [ "1234a56b7c89d012345e678f", "507f1f77bcf86cd799439011" ]
  }]
}
```

#### removeRoleAttribute

Removes a role attribute from the team.

##### Parameters

- `key`: The role attribute key to remove.

Here's an example:
```json
{
  "instructions": [
    {
      "kind": "removeRoleAttribute",
      "key": "testAttribute"
    }
  ]
}
```

#### replaceMembers

Replaces the existing members of the team with the new members.

##### Parameters

- `values`: List of member IDs of the new members.

Here's an example:

```json
{
  "instructions": [{
    "kind": "replaceMembers",
    "values": [ "1234a56b7c89d012345e678f", "507f1f77bcf86cd799439011" ]
  }]
}
```

#### replaceRoleAttributes

Replaces the existing role attributes for the team with new role attributes.

##### Parameters

- `value`: A map of role attribute keys to lists of role attribute values

Here's an example:

```json
{
  "instructions": [{
    "kind": "replaceRoleAttributes",
    "value": {
      "testAttribute": [ "someNewValue", "someOtherNewValue" ],
      "projectRoleAttribute": [ "project1", "project2"]
    }
  }]
}
```

#### updateDescription

Updates the description of the team.

##### Parameters

- `value`: The new description.

Here's an example:

```json
{
  "instructions": [{
    "kind": "updateDescription",
    "value": "Updated team description"
  }]
}
```

#### updateName

Updates the name of the team.

##### Parameters

- `value`: The new name.

Here's an example:

```json
{
  "instructions": [{
    "kind": "updateName",
    "value": "Updated team name"
  }]
}
```

#### updateRoleAttribute

Updates a role attribute on the team. Any existing values for the given key will be replaced with the new values. Team members will have these role attribute values scoped for all custom roles granted to them.

##### Parameters

- `key`: The role attribute key to update.
- `values`: List of role attribute values for that key.

Here's an example:
```json
{
  "instructions": [
    {
      "kind": "updateRoleAttribute",
      "key": "testAttribute",
      "values": ["someNewValue", "someOtherNewValue"]
    }
  ]
}
```

</details>

### Expanding the teams response
LaunchDarkly supports four fields for expanding the "Update team" response. By default, these fields are **not** included in the response.

To expand the response, append the `expand` query parameter and add a comma-separated list with any of the following fields:

* `members` includes the total count of members that belong to the team.
* `roles` includes a paginated list of the custom roles that you have assigned to the team.
* `projects` includes a paginated list of the projects that the team has any write access to.
* `maintainers` includes a paginated list of the maintainers that you have assigned to the team.

For example, `expand=members,roles` includes the `members` and `roles` fields in the response.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "comment": "Optional comment about the update",
  "instructions": [
    {
      "kind": "updateDescription",
      "value": "New description for the team"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="update-team-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|teamKey|path|string(string)|true|The team key|
|expand|query|string(string)|false|A comma-separated list of properties that can reveal additional information in the response. Supported fields are explained above.|
|body|body|[teamPatchInput](#schemateampatchinput)|true|none|
|» comment|body|string|false|Optional comment describing the update|
|» instructions|body|[Instructions](#schemainstructions)|true|The instructions to perform when updating. This should be an array with objects that look like <code>{"kind": "update_action"}</code>. Some instructions also require additional parameters as part of this object.|

## Add multiple members to team

<a id="opIdpostTeamMembers"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://app.launchdarkly.com/api/v2/teams/string/members \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -F 'file=@/path/to/file'
```

`POST /api/v2/teams/{teamKey}/members`

Add multiple members to an existing team by uploading a CSV file of member email addresses. Your CSV file must include email addresses in the first column. You can include data in additional columns, but LaunchDarkly ignores all data outside the first column. Headers are optional. To learn more, read [Manage team members](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/account/manage-teams#manage-team-members).

**Members are only added on a `201` response.** A `207` indicates the CSV file contains a combination of valid and invalid entries. A `207` results in no members being added to the team.

On a `207` response, if an entry contains bad input, the `message` field contains the row number as well as the reason for the error. The `message` field is omitted if the entry is valid.

Example `207` response:
```json
{
  "items": [
    {
      "status": "success",
      "value": "new-team-member@acme.com"
    },
    {
      "message": "Line 2: empty row",
      "status": "error",
      "value": ""
    },
    {
      "message": "Line 3: email already exists in the specified team",
      "status": "error",
      "value": "existing-team-member@acme.com"
    },
    {
      "message": "Line 4: invalid email formatting",
      "status": "error",
      "value": "invalid email format"
    }
  ]
}
```

Message | Resolution
--- | ---
Empty row | This line is blank. Add an email address and try again.
Duplicate entry | This email address appears in the file twice. Remove the email from the file and try again.
Email already exists in the specified team | This member is already on your team. Remove the email from the file and try again.
Invalid formatting | This email address is not formatted correctly. Fix the formatting and try again.
Email does not belong to a LaunchDarkly member | The email address doesn't belong to a LaunchDarkly account member. Invite them to LaunchDarkly, then re-add them to the team.

On a `400` response, the `message` field may contain errors specific to this endpoint.

Example `400` response:
```json
{
  "code": "invalid_request",
  "message": "Unable to process file"
}
```

Message | Resolution
--- | ---
Unable to process file | LaunchDarkly could not process the file for an unspecified reason. Review your file for errors and try again.
File exceeds 25mb | Break up your file into multiple files of less than 25mbs each.
All emails have invalid formatting | None of the email addresses in the file are in the correct format. Fix the formatting and try again.
All emails belong to existing team members | All listed members are already on this team. Populate the file with member emails that do not belong to the team and try again.
File is empty | The CSV file does not contain any email addresses. Populate the file and try again.
No emails belong to members of your LaunchDarkly organization | None of the email addresses belong to members of your LaunchDarkly account. Invite these members to LaunchDarkly, then re-add them to the team.


> Body parameter

```yaml
file: string
```

<h3 id="add-multiple-members-to-team-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|teamKey|path|string(string)|true|The team key|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» file|body|string(binary)|false|CSV file containing email addresses|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "items": [
    {
      "message": "string",
      "status": "error",
      "value": "new-team-member@acme.com"
    }
  ]
}
```

```json

    }
  ]
}
```

```json
  "code": "invalid_request",
  "message": "Invalid request body"
}
```

```json
  "code": "unauthorized",

}
```

```json

}
```

```json
}
```

<h1 id="launchdarkly-rest-api-teams-beta">Teams (beta)</h1>

> ### This feature is in beta
>
> To use this feature, pass in a header including the `LD-API-Version` key with value set to `beta`. Use this header with each call. To learn more, read [Beta resources](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/api#beta-resources).
>
> Resources that are in beta are still undergoing testing and development. They may change without notice, including becoming backwards incompatible.

> ### Teams is an Enterprise feature
>
> Teams is available to customers on an Enterprise plan. To learn more, [read about our pricing](https://launchdarkly.com/pricing/). To upgrade your plan, [contact Sales](https://launchdarkly.com/contact-sales/).

A team is a group of members in your LaunchDarkly account. A team can have maintainers who are able to add and remove team members. It also can have custom roles assigned to it that allows shared access to those roles for all team members. To learn more, read [Teams](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/account/teams).


## Update teams

<a id="opIdpatchTeams"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://app.launchdarkly.com/api/v2/teams \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "comment": "Optional comment about the update",
    "instructions": [
      {
        "kind": "addMembersToTeams",
        "memberIDs": [
          "1234a56b7c89d012345e678f"
        ],
        "teamKeys": [
          "example-team-1",
          "example-team-2"
        ]
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`PATCH /api/v2/teams`

Perform a partial update to multiple teams. Updating teams uses the semantic patch format.

To make a semantic patch request, you must append `domain-model=launchdarkly.semanticpatch` to your `Content-Type` header. To learn more, read [Updates using semantic patch](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/api#updates-using-semantic-patch).

### Instructions

Semantic patch requests support the following `kind` instructions for updating teams.

<details>
<summary>Click to expand instructions for <strong>updating teams</strong></summary>

#### addMembersToTeams

Add the members to teams.

##### Parameters

- `memberIDs`: List of member IDs to add.
- `teamKeys`: List of teams to update.

Here's an example:

```json
{
  "instructions": [{
    "kind": "addMembersToTeams",
    "memberIDs": [
      "1234a56b7c89d012345e678f"
    ],
    "teamKeys": [
      "example-team-1",
      "example-team-2"
    ]
  }]
}
```

#### addAllMembersToTeams

Add all members to the team. Members that match any of the filters are **excluded** from the update.

##### Parameters

- `teamKeys`: List of teams to update.
- `filterLastSeen`: (Optional) A JSON object with one of the following formats:
  - `{"never": true}` - Members that have never been active, such as those who have not accepted their invitation to LaunchDarkly, or have not logged in after being provisioned via SCIM.
  - `{"noData": true}` - Members that have not been active since LaunchDarkly began recording last seen timestamps.
  - `{"before": 1608672063611}` - Members that have not been active since the provided value, which should be a timestamp in Unix epoch milliseconds.
- `filterQuery`: (Optional) A string that matches against the members' emails and names. It is not case sensitive.
- `filterRoles`: (Optional) A `|` separated list of roles and custom roles. For the purposes of this filtering, `Owner` counts as `Admin`.
- `filterTeamKey`: (Optional) A string that matches against the key of the team the members belong to. It is not case sensitive.
- `ignoredMemberIDs`: (Optional) A list of member IDs.

Here's an example:

```json
{
  "instructions": [{
    "kind": "addAllMembersToTeams",
    "teamKeys": [
      "example-team-1",
      "example-team-2"
    ],
    "filterLastSeen": { "never": true }
  }]
}
```

</details>


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "comment": "Optional comment about the update",
  "instructions": [
    {
      "kind": "addMembersToTeams",
      "memberIDs": [
        "1234a56b7c89d012345e678f"
      ],
      "teamKeys": [
        "example-team-1",
        "example-team-2"
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="update-teams-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[teamsPatchInput](#schemateamspatchinput)|true|none|
|» comment|body|string|false|Optional comment describing the update|
|» instructions|body|[Instructions](#schemainstructions)|true|The instructions to perform when updating. This should be an array with objects that look like <code>{"kind": "update_action"}</code>. Some instructions also require additional parameters as part of this object.|

```json
      "example-team-2": "example failure message"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h1 id="launchdarkly-rest-api-user-settings">User settings</h1>

> ### Contexts are now available
>
> After you have upgraded your LaunchDarkly SDK to use contexts instead of users, you should use [Contexts](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/api/contexts) instead of the user settings API. To learn more, read [Contexts](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/observability/contexts).

LaunchDarkly's user settings API provides a picture of all feature flags and their current values for a specific user. This gives you instant visibility into how a particular user experiences your site or application. To learn more, read [View and manage contexts](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/observability/context-attributes#view-and-manage-contexts).

You can also use the user settings API to assign a user to a specific variation for any feature flag.

## Update flag settings for user

<a id="opIdputFlagSetting"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://app.launchdarkly.com/api/v2/users/string/string/string/flags/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "setting": "existing_variation_value_to_use",
    "comment": "make sure this context experiences a specific variation"
  }'
```

`PUT /api/v2/users/{projectKey}/{environmentKey}/{userKey}/flags/{featureFlagKey}`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

Enable or disable a feature flag for a user based on their key.

Omitting the `setting` attribute from the request body, or including a `setting` of `null`, erases the current setting for a user.

If you previously patched the flag, and the patch included the user's data, LaunchDarkly continues to use that data. If LaunchDarkly has never encountered the user's key before, it calculates the flag values based on the user key alone.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "setting": "existing_variation_value_to_use",
  "comment": "make sure this context experiences a specific variation"
}
```

|userKey|path|string(string)|true|The user key|
|featureFlagKey|path|string(string)|true|The feature flag key|
|body|body|[ValuePut](#schemavalueput)|true|none|
|» setting|body|object|false|The variation value to set for the context. Must match the flag's variation type.|

## Update expiring user target for flags

<a id="opIdpatchExpiringFlagsForUser"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://app.launchdarkly.com/api/v2/users/string/string/expiring-user-targets/string \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "comment": "optional comment",
    "instructions": [
      {
        "kind": "addExpireUserTargetDate",
        "flagKey": "sample-flag-key",
        "variationId": "ce12d345-a1b2-4fb5-a123-ab123d4d5f5d",
        "value": 1653469200000,
        "version": 1
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`PATCH /api/v2/users/{projectKey}/{userKey}/expiring-user-targets/{environmentKey}`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

Schedule the specified user for removal from individual targeting on one or more flags. The user must already be individually targeted for each flag.

You can add, update, or remove a scheduled removal date. You can only schedule a user for removal on a single variation per flag.

Updating an expiring target uses the semantic patch format. To make a semantic patch request, you must append `domain-model=launchdarkly.semanticpatch` to your `Content-Type` header. To learn more, read [Updates using semantic patch](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/api#updates-using-semantic-patch).

### Instructions

Semantic patch requests support the following `kind` instructions for updating expiring user targets.

<details>
<summary>Click to expand instructions for <strong>updating expiring user targets</strong></summary>

#### addExpireUserTargetDate

Adds a date and time that LaunchDarkly will remove the user from the flag's individual targeting.

##### Parameters

* `flagKey`: The flag key
* `variationId`: ID of a variation on the flag
* `value`: The time, in Unix milliseconds, when LaunchDarkly should remove the user from individual targeting for this flag.

#### updateExpireUserTargetDate

Updates the date and time that LaunchDarkly will remove the user from the flag's individual targeting.

##### Parameters

* `flagKey`: The flag key
* `variationId`: ID of a variation on the flag
* `value`: The time, in Unix milliseconds, when LaunchDarkly should remove the user from individual targeting for this flag.
* `version`: The version of the expiring user target to update. If included, update will fail if version doesn't match current version of the expiring user target.

#### removeExpireUserTargetDate

Removes the scheduled removal of the user from the flag's individual targeting. The user will remain part of the flag's individual targeting until explicitly removed, or until another removal is scheduled.

##### Parameters

* `flagKey`: The flag key
* `variationId`: ID of a variation on the flag

</details>


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "comment": "optional comment",
  "instructions": [
    {
      "kind": "addExpireUserTargetDate",
      "flagKey": "sample-flag-key",
      "variationId": "ce12d345-a1b2-4fb5-a123-ab123d4d5f5d",
      "value": 1653469200000,
      "version": 1
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="update-expiring-user-target-for-flags-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|projectKey|path|string(string)|true|The project key|
|userKey|path|string(string)|true|The user key|
|environmentKey|path|string(string)|true|The environment key|
|body|body|[patchUsersRequest](#schemapatchusersrequest)|true|none|
|» comment|body|string|false|Optional comment describing the change|
|» instructions|body|[[instructionUserRequest](#schemainstructionuserrequest)]|true|The instructions to perform when updating|

<h1 id="launchdarkly-rest-api-users">Users</h1>

> ### Contexts are now available
>
> After you have upgraded your LaunchDarkly SDK to use contexts instead of users, you should use [Contexts](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/api/contexts) instead of these endpoints. To learn more, read [Contexts](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/observability/contexts).


LaunchDarkly creates a record for each user passed in to `variation` calls. This record powers the autocomplete functionality on the feature flag dashboard, as well as the Users page. To learn more, read [Contexts](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/observability/contexts).

LaunchDarkly also offers an API that lets you tap into this data. You can use the users API to see what user data is available to LaunchDarkly, as well as determine which flag values a user will receive. You can also explicitly set which flag value a user will receive via this API.

Users are always scoped within a project and environment. In other words, each environment has its own set of user records.


## Find users

<a id="opIdgetSearchUsers"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://app.launchdarkly.com/api/v2/user-search/string/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /api/v2/user-search/{projectKey}/{environmentKey}`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

> ### Use contexts instead
>
> After you have upgraded your LaunchDarkly SDK to use contexts instead of users, you should use [Search for contexts](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/api/contexts/search-contexts) instead of this endpoint.

Search users in LaunchDarkly based on their last active date, a user attribute filter set, or a search query.

An example user attribute filter set is `filter=firstName:Anna,activeTrial:false`. This matches users that have the user attribute `firstName` set to `Anna`, that also have the attribute `activeTrial` set to `false`.

To paginate through results, follow the `next` link in the `_links` object. To learn more, read [Representations](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/api#representations).


<h3 id="find-users-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|projectKey|path|string(string)|true|The project key|
|environmentKey|path|string(string)|true|The environment key|
|q|query|string(string)|false|Full-text search for users based on name, first name, last name, e-mail address, or key|
|limit|query|integer(int64)|false|Specifies the maximum number of items in the collection to return (max: 50, default: 20)|
|searchAfter|query|string(string)|false|Limits results to users with sort values after the value you specify. You can use this for pagination, but we recommend using the `next` link we provide instead.|
|filter|query|string(string)|false|A comma-separated list of user attribute filters. Each filter is in the form of attributeKey:attributeValue|

## Get user

<a id="opIdgetUser"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://app.launchdarkly.com/api/v2/users/string/string/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /api/v2/users/{projectKey}/{environmentKey}/{userKey}`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

> ### Use contexts instead
>
> After you have upgraded your LaunchDarkly SDK to use contexts instead of users, you should use [Get contexts](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/api/contexts/get-contexts) instead of this endpoint.

Get a user by key. The `user` object contains all attributes sent in `variation` calls for that key.


<h3 id="get-user-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|projectKey|path|string(string)|true|The project key|
|environmentKey|path|string(string)|true|The environment key|
|userKey|path|string(string)|true|The user key|

<h1 id="launchdarkly-rest-api-views">Views</h1>

The views API allows you to create, retrieve, and edit views, and link other resources to views.

A view is a resource in LaunchDarkly that you can use to logically group other resources within a project, such as flags or segments. For example, views let you restrict access to sets of flags, so that members of your organization can focus on just the flags they work with.

To learn more, read [Views](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/account/views).


## List views

<a id="opIdgetViews"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://app.launchdarkly.com/api/v2/projects/default/views \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /api/v2/projects/{projectKey}/views`

Get a list of all views in the given project.

<h3 id="list-views-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|projectKey|path|string|true|none|
|sort|query|string|false|A sort to apply to the list of views.|
|limit|query|integer|false|The number of views to return.|
|offset|query|integer|false|Where to start in the list. Use this with pagination. For example, an offset of 10 skips the first ten items and then returns the next items in the list, up to the query `limit`.|
|filter|query|string|false|A filter to apply to the list of views. Supports the following fields and operators: `name` (equals, notEquals, startsWith, contains, anyOf), `key` (equals, notEquals, startsWith, contains, anyOf), `tag` (equals, anyOf), `maintainerId` (equals, anyOf), `isPayloadView` (equals).|
|expand|query|[string]|false|A comma-separated list of fields to expand.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|sort|key|
|sort|name|
|sort|updatedAt|
|expand|flagsSummary|
|expand|segmentsSummary|
|expand|metricsSummary|
|expand|aiConfigsSummary|
|expand|resourceSummary|

<h3 id="list-views-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Successful response|[Views](#schemaviews)|
|400|Bad Request|Bad request|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|404|Not Found|Not found|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|500|Internal Server Error|Internal server error|[Error](#schemaerror)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
ApiKey
</aside>

## Create view

<a id="opIdcreateView"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://app.launchdarkly.com/api/v2/projects/default/views \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "maintainerId": "maintainerId",
    "name": "name",
    "maintainerTeamKey": "maintainerTeamKey",
    "description": "",
    "key": "key",
    "tags": [
      "tags",
      "tags"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /api/v2/projects/{projectKey}/views`

Create a new view in the given project.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "maintainerId": "maintainerId",
  "name": "name",
  "maintainerTeamKey": "maintainerTeamKey",
  "description": "",
  "key": "key",
  "tags": [
    "tags",
    "tags"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-view-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|projectKey|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|[ViewPost](#schemaviewpost)|true|View object to create|
|» key|body|string|true|Unique key for the view within the account/project. The key is converted to lowercase when the view is created, so use the lowercase form to reference the view afterward.|
|» name|body|string|true|Human-readable name for the view|
|» description|body|string|false|Optional detailed description of the view|
|» maintainerId|body|string|false|Member ID of the maintainer for this view. Only one of `maintainerId` or `maintainerTeamKey` can be specified.|
|» maintainerTeamKey|body|string|false|Key of the maintainer team for this view. Only one of `maintainerId` or `maintainerTeamKey` can be specified.|
|» tags|body|[string]|false|Tags associated with this view|

<h3 id="create-view-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Successful response|[View](#schemaview)|
|400|Bad Request|Bad request|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|404|Not Found|Not found|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|500|Internal Server Error|Internal server error|[Error](#schemaerror)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
ApiKey
</aside>

## Get view

<a id="opIdgetView"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://app.launchdarkly.com/api/v2/projects/default/views/my-view \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /api/v2/projects/{projectKey}/views/{viewKey}`

Retrieve a specific view by its key.

<h3 id="get-view-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|projectKey|path|string|true|none|
|viewKey|path|string|true|none|
|sort|query|string|false|A sort to apply to the list of views.|
|limit|query|integer|false|The number of views to return.|
|offset|query|integer|false|Where to start in the list. Use this with pagination. For example, an offset of 10 skips the first ten items and then returns the next items in the list, up to the query `limit`.|
|filter|query|string|false|A filter to apply to the list of views. Supports the following fields and operators: `name` (equals, notEquals, startsWith, contains, anyOf), `key` (equals, notEquals, startsWith, contains, anyOf), `tag` (equals, anyOf), `maintainerId` (equals, anyOf), `isPayloadView` (equals).|
|expand|query|[string]|false|A comma-separated list of fields to expand.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|sort|key|
|sort|name|
|sort|updatedAt|
|expand|allFlags|
|expand|allSegments|
|expand|allMetrics|
|expand|allAIConfigs|
|expand|allResources|
|expand|maintainer|
|expand|flagsSummary|
|expand|segmentsSummary|
|expand|metricsSummary|
|expand|aiConfigsSummary|
|expand|resourceSummary|

```bash
curl https://app.launchdarkly.com/api/v2/projects/default/views/my-view \
  -X DELETE \

  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`DELETE /api/v2/projects/{projectKey}/views/{viewKey}`

## Update view

<a id="opIdupdateView"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://app.launchdarkly.com/api/v2/projects/default/views/my-view \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "maintainerId": "maintainerId",
    "name": "name",
    "maintainerTeamKey": "maintainerTeamKey",
    "description": "description",
    "tags": [
      "tags",
      "tags"
    ]
  }'
```

`PATCH /api/v2/projects/{projectKey}/views/{viewKey}`

Edit an existing view.

The request body must be a JSON object of the fields to update. The values you include replace the existing values for the fields.

Here's an example:
  ```
    {
      "description": "Example updated description",
      "tags": ["new-tag"]
    }
  ```


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "maintainerId": "maintainerId",
  "name": "name",
  "maintainerTeamKey": "maintainerTeamKey",
  "description": "description",
  "tags": [
    "tags",
    "tags"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="update-view-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|projectKey|path|string|true|none|
|viewKey|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|[ViewPatch](#schemaviewpatch)|true|A JSON representation of the view including only the fields to update.|
|» name|body|string|false|Human-readable name for the view|
|» description|body|string|false|Optional detailed description of the view|
|» maintainerId|body|string|false|Member ID of the maintainer for this view. Only one of `maintainerId` or `maintainerTeamKey` can be specified.|
|» maintainerTeamKey|body|string|false|Key of the maintainer team for this view. Only one of `maintainerId` or `maintainerTeamKey` can be specified.|
|» tags|body|[string]|false|Tags associated with this view|

## Link resource

<a id="opIdlinkResource"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://app.launchdarkly.com/api/v2/projects/default/views/my-view/link/flags \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "filter": "maintainerId:507f1f77bcf86cd799439011,tags:backend+beta",
    "keys": [
      "flag-1",
      "flag-2"
    ],
    "comment": ""
  }'
```

`POST /api/v2/projects/{projectKey}/views/{viewKey}/link/{resourceType}`

Link one or multiple resources to a view by keys, filters, or both:
- Link flags using flag keys or filters (maintainerId, maintainerTeamKey, tags, state, query)
- Link segments using segment IDs or filters (tags, query, unbounded)
- Link AI configs using config keys

When both keys and filters are provided, resources matching either condition are linked (union).


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "filter": "maintainerId:507f1f77bcf86cd799439011,tags:backend+beta",
  "keys": [
    "flag-1",
    "flag-2"
  ],
  "comment": ""
}
```

<h3 id="link-resource-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|projectKey|path|string|true|none|
|viewKey|path|string|true|none|
|resourceType|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|[ViewLinkRequest](#schemaviewlinkrequest)|true|Resources to link to the view. You can provide explicit keys/IDs, filters, or both.<br>- Flags: identified by key or filtered by maintainerId, maintainerTeamKey, tags, state, query<br>- Segments: identified by segment ID or filtered by tags, query, unbounded<br>|
|» *oneOf*|body|[ViewLinkRequestKeys](#schemaviewlinkrequestkeys)|false|none|
|» *oneOf*|body|[ViewLinkRequestSegmentIdentifiers](#schemaviewlinkrequestsegmentidentifiers)|false|none|
|» *oneOf*|body|[ViewLinkRequestFilter](#schemaviewlinkrequestfilter)|false|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|resourceType|flags|
|resourceType|segments|
|resourceType|aiConfigs|

## Unlink resource

<a id="opIdunlinkResource"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://app.launchdarkly.com/api/v2/projects/default/views/my-view/link/flags \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "filter": "maintainerId:507f1f77bcf86cd799439011,tags:backend+beta",
    "keys": [
      "flag-1",
      "flag-2"
    ],
    "comment": ""
  }'
```

`DELETE /api/v2/projects/{projectKey}/views/{viewKey}/link/{resourceType}`

Unlink one or multiple resources from a view:
- Unlink flags using flag keys
- Unlink segments using segment IDs
- Unlink AI configs using config keys


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "filter": "maintainerId:507f1f77bcf86cd799439011,tags:backend+beta",
  "keys": [
    "flag-1",
    "flag-2"
  ],
  "comment": ""
}
```

<h3 id="unlink-resource-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|projectKey|path|string|true|none|
|viewKey|path|string|true|none|
|resourceType|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|[ViewLinkRequest](#schemaviewlinkrequest)|true|The resource to link to the view. Flags are identified by key. Segments are identified by segment ID.|
|» *oneOf*|body|[ViewLinkRequestKeys](#schemaviewlinkrequestkeys)|false|none|
|» *oneOf*|body|[ViewLinkRequestSegmentIdentifiers](#schemaviewlinkrequestsegmentidentifiers)|false|none|
|» *oneOf*|body|[ViewLinkRequestFilter](#schemaviewlinkrequestfilter)|false|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|resourceType|flags|
|resourceType|segments|
|resourceType|aiConfigs|

## Get linked resources

<a id="opIdgetLinkedResources"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://app.launchdarkly.com/api/v2/projects/default/views/my-view/linked/flags \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /api/v2/projects/{projectKey}/views/{viewKey}/linked/{resourceType}`

Get a list of all linked resources for a given view.

<h3 id="get-linked-resources-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|projectKey|path|string|true|none|
|viewKey|path|string|true|none|
|resourceType|path|string|true|none|
|limit|query|integer|false|The number of views to return.|
|offset|query|integer|false|Where to start in the list. Use this with pagination. For example, an offset of 10 skips the first ten items and then returns the next items in the list, up to the query `limit`.|
|sort|query|string|false|Field to sort by. Default field is `linkedAt`, default order is ascending.|
|query|query|string|false|Case-insensitive search query for linked resources. Matches resource key and, when expanded, resource name.|
|filter|query|string|false|Optional resource filter expression for linked resources.<br>- Supported for `flags` and `segments` resource types.<br>- Uses the same syntax as link/unlink and list endpoints.<br>- For `segments`, `environmentId` is required when `filter` is provided.<br>|
|expand|query|[string]|false|A comma-separated list of fields to expand.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|resourceType|flags|
|resourceType|segments|
|resourceType|aiConfigs|
|sort|linkedAt|
|sort|name|
|expand|maintainer|
|expand|resourceDetails|

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Successful response|[ViewLinkedResources](#schemaviewlinkedresources)|
|400|Bad Request|Bad request|[Error](#schemaerror)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
ApiKey
</aside>

## Get linked views for a given resource

<a id="opIdgetLinkedViews"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://app.launchdarkly.com/api/v2/projects/default/view-associations/flags/my-flag \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /api/v2/projects/{projectKey}/view-associations/{resourceType}/{resourceKey}`

Get a list of all linked views for a resource. Flags and AI configs are identified by key. Segments are identified by segment ID.

<h3 id="get-linked-views-for-a-given-resource-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|projectKey|path|string|true|none|
|resourceType|path|string|true|none|
|resourceKey|path|string|true|none|
|environmentId|query|string|false|Environment ID. Required when resourceType is 'segments'|
|limit|query|integer|false|The number of views to return.|
|offset|query|integer|false|Where to start in the list. Use this with pagination. For example, an offset of 10 skips the first ten items and then returns the next items in the list, up to the query `limit`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|resourceType|flags|
|resourceType|segments|
|resourceType|aiConfigs|

<h1 id="launchdarkly-rest-api-webhooks">Webhooks</h1>

The webhooks API lets you build your own integrations that subscribe to activities in LaunchDarkly. When you generate an activity in LaunchDarkly, such as when you change a flag or you create a project, LaunchDarkly sends an HTTP POST payload to the webhook's URL. Use webhooks to update external issue trackers, update support tickets, notify customers of new feature rollouts, and more.

Several of the endpoints in the webhooks API require a webhook ID. The webhook ID is returned as part of the [Creates a webhook](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/api/webhooks/post-webhook) and [List webhooks](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/api/webhooks/get-all-webhooks) responses. It is the `_id` field, or the `_id` field of each element in the `items` array.

## Designating the payload

The webhook payload is identical to an audit log entry. To learn more, read [Get audit log entry](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/api/audit-log/get-audit-log-entry).

Here's a sample payload:

> ### Webhook delivery order
>
> Webhooks may not be delivered in chronological order. We recommend using the payload's "date" field as a timestamp to reorder webhooks as they are received.

```json
{
  "_links": {
    "canonical": {
      "href": "/api/v2/projects/alexis/environments/test",
      "type": "application/json"
    },
    "parent": {
      "href": "/api/v2/auditlog",
      "type": "application/json"
    },
    "self": {
      "href": "/api/v2/auditlog/57c0a8e29969090743529965",
      "type": "application/json"
    },
    "site": {
      "href": "/settings#/projects",
      "type": "text/html"
    }
  },
  "_id": "57c0a8e29969090743529965",
  "date": 1472243938774,
  "accesses": [
    {
      "action": "updateName",
      "resource": "proj/alexis:env/test"
    }
  ],
  "kind": "environment",
  "name": "Testing",
  "description": "- Changed the name from ~~Test~~ to *Testing*",
  "member": {
    "_links": {
      "parent": {
        "href": "/internal/account/members",
        "type": "application/json"
      },
      "self": {
        "href": "/internal/account/members/548f6741c1efad40031b18ae",
        "type": "application/json"
      }
    },
    "_id": "548f6741c1efad40031b18ae",
    "email": "ariel@acme.com",
    "firstName": "Ariel",
    "lastName": "Flores"
  },
  "titleVerb": "changed the name of",
  "title": "[Ariel Flores](mailto:ariel@acme.com) changed the name of [Testing](https://app.launchdarkly.com/settings#/projects)",
  "target": {
    "_links": {
      "canonical": {
        "href": "/api/v2/projects/alexis/environments/test",
        "type": "application/json"
      },
      "site": {
        "href": "/settings#/projects",
        "type": "text/html"
      }
    },
    "name": "Testing",
    "resources": ["proj/alexis:env/test"]
  }
}
```

## Signing the webhook

Optionally, you can define a `secret` when you create a webhook. If you define the secret, the webhook `POST` request will include an `X-LD-Signature header`, whose value will contain an HMAC SHA256 hex digest of the webhook payload, using the `secret` as the key.

Compute the signature of the payload using the same shared secret in your code to verify that the webhook was triggered by LaunchDarkly.

## Understanding connection retries

If LaunchDarkly receives a non-`2xx` response to a webhook `POST`, it will retry the delivery one time. Webhook delivery is not guaranteed. If you build an integration on webhooks, make sure it is tolerant of delivery failures.

## Creates a webhook

<a id="opIdpostWebhook"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://app.launchdarkly.com/api/v2/webhooks \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "apidocs test webhook",
    "on": true,
    "sign": false,
    "statements": [
      {
        "actions": [
          "*"
        ],
        "effect": "allow",
        "resources": [
          "proj/test"
        ]
      }
    ],
    "tags": [
      "example-tag"
    ],
    "url": "https://example.com"
  }'
```

`POST /api/v2/webhooks`

Create a new webhook.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "apidocs test webhook",
  "on": true,
  "sign": false,
  "statements": [
    {
      "actions": [
        "*"
      ],
      "effect": "allow",
      "resources": [
        "proj/test"
      ]
    }
  ],
  "tags": [
    "example-tag"
  ],
  "url": "https://example.com"
}
```

<h3 id="creates-a-webhook-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[webhookPost](#schemawebhookpost)|true|none|
|» name|body|string|false|A human-readable name for your webhook|
|» url|body|string|true|The URL of the remote webhook|

<h1 id="launchdarkly-rest-api-workflow-templates">Workflow templates</h1>

> ### Workflows are in maintenance mode
>
> The workflows feature is in maintenance mode, and is planned for future deprecation at a date not yet specified. We will work with existing customers using workflows to migrate to a replacement solution when deprecation occurs.

Workflow templates allow you to define a set of workflow stages that you can use as a starting point for new workflows. You can create these workflows for any flag in any environment and any project, and you can create as many workflows as you like from a given template.

You can create workflow templates in two ways:
* by specifying the desired stages, using the `stages` property of the request body
* by specifying an existing workflow to save as a template, using the `workflowId` property of the request body

You can use templates to create a workflow in any project, environment, or flag. However, when you create a template, you must specify a particular project, environment, and flag. This means that when you create a template using the `stages` property, you must also include `projectKey`, `environmentKey`, and `flagKey` properties in the request body. When you create a template from an existing workflow, it will use the project, environment, and flag of the existing workflow, so those properties can be omitted from the request body.

To learn more, read [Workflows documentation](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/releases/workflows) and [Workflows API documentation](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/api/workflows).

<h1 id="launchdarkly-rest-api-workflows">Workflows</h1>

> ### Workflows are in maintenance mode
>
> The workflows feature is in maintenance mode, and is planned for future deprecation at a date not yet specified. We will work with existing customers using workflows to migrate to a replacement solution when deprecation occurs.

A workflow is a set of actions that you can schedule in advance to make changes to a feature flag at a future date and time. You can also include approval requests at different stages of a workflow. To learn more, read [Workflows](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/releases/workflows).

The actions supported are as follows:

- Turning targeting `ON` or `OFF`
- Setting the default variation
- Adding targets to a given variation
- Creating a rule to target by segment
- Modifying the rollout percentage for rules

You can create multiple stages of a flag release workflow. Unique stages are defined by their conditions: either approvals and/or scheduled changes.

Several of the endpoints in the workflows API require a workflow ID or one or more member IDs. The workflow ID is returned as part of the [Create workflow](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/api/workflows/post-workflow) and [Get workflows](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/api/workflows/get-workflows) responses. It is the `_id` field, or the `_id` field of each element in the `items` array. The member ID is returned as part of the [List account members](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/api/account-members/get-members) response. It is the `_id` field of each element in the `items` array.


## Get workflows

<a id="opIdgetWorkflows"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://app.launchdarkly.com/api/v2/projects/string/flags/string/environments/string/workflows \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /api/v2/projects/{projectKey}/flags/{featureFlagKey}/environments/{environmentKey}/workflows`

Display workflows associated with a feature flag.

<h3 id="get-workflows-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|projectKey|path|string(string)|true|The project key|
|featureFlagKey|path|string(string)|true|The feature flag key|
|environmentKey|path|string(string)|true|The environment key|
|status|query|string(string)|false|Filter results by workflow status. Valid status filters are `active`, `completed`, and `failed`.|
|sort|query|string(string)|false|A field to sort the items by. Prefix field by a dash ( - ) to sort in descending order. This endpoint supports sorting by `creationDate` or `stopDate`.|
|limit|query|integer(int64)|false|The maximum number of workflows to return. Defaults to 20.|
|offset|query|integer(int64)|false|Where to start in the list. Defaults to 0. Use this with pagination. For example, an offset of 10 skips the first ten items and then returns the next items in the list, up to the query `limit`.|

## Create workflow

<a id="opIdpostWorkflow"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://app.launchdarkly.com/api/v2/projects/string/flags/string/environments/string/workflows \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "description": "Turn flag on for 10% of customers each day",
    "name": "Progressive rollout starting in two days",
    "stages": [
      {
        "action": {
          "instructions": [
            {
              "kind": "turnFlagOn"
            },
            {
              "kind": "updateFallthroughVariationOrRollout",
              "rolloutWeights": {
                "452f5fb5-7320-4ba3-81a1-8f4324f79d49": 90000,
                "fc15f6a4-05d3-4aa4-a997-446be461345d": 10000
              }
            }
          ]
        },
        "conditions": [
          {
            "kind": "schedule",
            "scheduleKind": "relative",
            "waitDuration": 2,
            "waitDurationUnit": "calendarDay"
          }
        ],
        "name": "10% rollout on day 1"
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /api/v2/projects/{projectKey}/flags/{featureFlagKey}/environments/{environmentKey}/workflows`

> ### Workflows are in maintenance mode
>
> The workflows feature is in maintenance mode, and is planned for future deprecation at a date not yet specified. We will work with existing customers using workflows to migrate to a replacement solution when deprecation occurs.

Create a workflow for a feature flag. You can create a workflow directly, or you can apply a template to create a new workflow.

### Creating a workflow

You can use the create workflow endpoint to create a workflow directly by adding a `stages` array to the request body.

For each stage, define the `name`, `conditions` when the stage should be executed, and `action` that describes the stage. For approval stages, only standard LaunchDarkly approvals are permitted. Workflows of `kind` `integration-approval` cannot be used for custom workflows. 

<details>
<summary>Click to expand example</summary>

_Example request body_
```json
{
  "name": "Progressive rollout starting in two days",
  "description": "Turn flag targeting on and increase feature rollout in 10% increments each day",
  "stages": [
    {
      "name": "10% rollout on day 1",
      "conditions": [
        {
          "kind": "schedule",
          "scheduleKind": "relative", // or "absolute"
              //  If "scheduleKind" is "absolute", set "executionDate";
              // "waitDuration" and "waitDurationUnit" will be ignored
          "waitDuration": 2,
          "waitDurationUnit": "calendarDay"
        },
        {
          "kind": "ld-approval",
          "notifyMemberIds": [ "507f1f77bcf86cd799439011" ],
          "notifyTeamKeys": [ "team-key-123abc" ]
        }
      ],
      "action": {
        "instructions": [
          {
            "kind": "turnFlagOn"
          },
          {
            "kind": "updateFallthroughVariationOrRollout",
            "rolloutWeights": {
              "452f5fb5-7320-4ba3-81a1-8f4324f79d49": 90000,
              "fc15f6a4-05d3-4aa4-a997-446be461345d": 10000
            }
          }
        ]
      }
    }
  ]
}
```
</details>

### Creating a workflow by applying a workflow template

You can also create a workflow by applying a workflow template. If you pass a valid workflow template key as the `templateKey` query parameter with the request, the API will attempt to create a new workflow with the stages defined in the workflow template with the corresponding key.

#### Applicability of stages
Templates are created in the context of a particular flag in a particular environment in a particular project. However, because workflows created from a template can be applied to any project, environment, and flag, some steps of the workflow may need to be updated in order to be applicable for the target resource.

You can pass a `dryRun` query parameter to tell the API to return a report of which steps of the workflow template are applicable in the target project/environment/flag, and which will need to be updated. When the `dryRun` query parameter is present the response body includes a `meta` property that holds a list of parameters that could potentially be inapplicable for the target resource. Each of these parameters will include a `valid` field. You will need to update any invalid parameters in order to create the new workflow. You can do this using the `parameters` property, which overrides the workflow template parameters.

#### Overriding template parameters
You can use the `parameters` property in the request body to tell the API to override the specified workflow template parameters with new values that are specific to your target project/environment/flag.

<details>
<summary>Click to expand example</summary>

_Example request body_
```json
{
	"name": "workflow created from my-template",
	"description": "description of my workflow",
	"parameters": [
		{
			"_id": "62cf2bc4cadbeb7697943f3b",
			"path": "/clauses/0/values",
			"default": {
				"value": ["updated-segment"]
			}
		},
		{
			"_id": "62cf2bc4cadbeb7697943f3d",
			"path": "/variationId",
			"default": {
				"value": "abcd1234-abcd-1234-abcd-1234abcd12"
			}
		}
	]
}
```
</details>

If there are any steps in the template that are not applicable to the target resource, the workflow will not be created, and the `meta` property will be included in the response body detailing which parameters need to be updated.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "description": "Turn flag on for 10% of customers each day",
  "name": "Progressive rollout starting in two days",
  "stages": [
    {
      "action": {
        "instructions": [
          {
            "kind": "turnFlagOn"
          },
          {
            "kind": "updateFallthroughVariationOrRollout",
            "rolloutWeights": {
              "452f5fb5-7320-4ba3-81a1-8f4324f79d49": 90000,
              "fc15f6a4-05d3-4aa4-a997-446be461345d": 10000
            }
          }
        ]
      },
      "conditions": [
        {
          "kind": "schedule",
          "scheduleKind": "relative",
          "waitDuration": 2,
          "waitDurationUnit": "calendarDay"
        }
      ],
      "name": "10% rollout on day 1"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-workflow-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|templateKey|query|string(string)|false|The template key to apply as a starting point for the new workflow|
|dryRun|query|boolean|false|Whether to call the endpoint in dry-run mode|
|projectKey|path|string(string)|true|The project key|
|featureFlagKey|path|string(string)|true|The feature flag key|
|environmentKey|path|string(string)|true|The environment key|
|body|body|[CustomWorkflowInput](#schemacustomworkflowinput)|true|none|
|» maintainerId|body|[ObjectId](#schemaobjectid)|false|The ID of the workflow maintainer. Defaults to the workflow creator.|
|» name|body|string|true|The workflow name|
|» description|body|string|false|The workflow description|
|» stages|body|[[StageInput](#schemastageinput)]|false|A list of the workflow stages|
|» templateKey|body|string|false|The template key|

```json
    "104.156.80.0/20",
    "151.101.0.0/16"
  ],
  "outboundAddresses": [
    "52.21.152.96/32"
  ]
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "code": "rate_limited",
  "message": "You've exceeded the API rate limit. Try again later."
}
```

<h3 id="gets-the-public-ip-list-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Public IP response|[ipList](#schemaiplist)|
|429|Too Many Requests|Rate limited|[RateLimitedErrorRep](#schemaratelimitederrorrep)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
ApiKey
</aside>

## Get version information

<a id="opIdgetVersions"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://app.launchdarkly.com/api/v2/versions \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /api/v2/versions`

Get the latest API version, the list of valid API versions in ascending order, and the version being used for this request. These are all in the external, date-based format.

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "validVersions": [
    0
  ],
  "latestVersion": "20220603",
  "currentVersion": "20220603",
  "beta": false
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "code": "unauthorized",
  "message": "Invalid access token"
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "code": "forbidden",
  "message": "Forbidden. Access to the requested resource was denied."
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "code": "rate_limited",
  "message": "You've exceeded the API rate limit. Try again later."
}
```

<h3 id="get-version-information-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Versions information response|[VersionsRep](#schemaversionsrep)|
|401|Unauthorized|Invalid access token|[UnauthorizedErrorRep](#schemaunauthorizederrorrep)|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden|[ForbiddenErrorRep](#schemaforbiddenerrorrep)|
|429|Too Many Requests|Rate limited|[RateLimitedErrorRep](#schemaratelimitederrorrep)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
ApiKey
</aside>

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|_links|object|true|none|The location and content type of related resources|
|_id|string|true|none|The ID for the environment. Use this as the client-side ID for authorization in some client-side SDKs, and to associate LaunchDarkly environments with CDN integrations in edge SDKs.|
|key|string|true|none|A project-unique key for the new environment|
|name|string|true|none|A human-friendly name for the new environment|
|apiKey|string|true|none|The SDK key for the environment. Use this for authorization in server-side SDKs.|
|mobileKey|string|true|none|The mobile key for the environment. Use this for authorization in mobile SDKs.|
|color|string|true|none|The color used to indicate this environment in the UI|
|defaultTtl|integer|true|none|The default time (in minutes) that the PHP SDK can cache feature flag rules locally|
|secureMode|boolean|true|none|Ensures that one end user of the client-side SDK cannot inspect the variations for another end user|
|_access|[Access](#schemaaccess)|false|none|none|
|defaultTrackEvents|boolean|true|none|The initial value of trackEvents for flags created in this environment. Does not affect existing flags. Required for Data Export, but doesn't enable Data Export on its own.|
|requireComments|boolean|true|none|Whether members who modify flags and segments through the LaunchDarkly user interface are required to add a comment|
|confirmChanges|boolean|true|none|Whether members who modify flags and segments through the LaunchDarkly user interface are required to confirm those changes|
|tags|[string]|true|none|A list of tags for this environment|
|approvalSettings|[ApprovalSettings](#schemaapprovalsettings)|false|none|Details about the approval settings for flags in this environment|
|resourceApprovalSettings|object|false|none|Details about the approval settings for other resources in this environment, organized by resource kind (for example, "aiconfig" and "segment")|
|critical|boolean|true|none|Whether the environment is critical|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|kind|string|true|none|Describes the general reason that LaunchDarkly selected this variation.|

|ruleID|string|false|none|The unique identifier of the matching rule if the kind is 'RULE_MATCH'.|
|prerequisiteKey|string|false|none|The key of the flag that failed if the kind is 'PREREQUISITE_FAILED'.|
|inExperiment|boolean|false|none|Indicates whether the evaluation occurred as part of an experiment.|
|errorKind|string|false|none|The specific error type if the kind is 'ERROR'.|

```json
{
  "type": "contextAttribute",
  "attribute": "country",
  "op": "in",
  "values": [
    "JP"
  ],
  "contextKind": "user",
  "negate": false

```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|type|string|true|none|Filter type. One of [contextAttribute, eventProperty, group]|
|attribute|string|false|none|If not a group node, the context attribute name or event property name to filter on|
|op|[Operator](#schemaoperator)|true|none|The function to perform|
|values|[object]|true|none|The context attribute / event property values or group member nodes. Numeric values must not exceed 14 decimal places.|
|contextKind|string|false|none|For context attribute filters, the context kind.|
|negate|boolean|true|none|If set, then take the inverse of the operator. 'in' becomes 'not in'.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|_id|string|true|none|The ID of this approval request|
|_version|integer|true|none|Version of the approval request|
|creationDate|[UnixMillis](#schemaunixmillis)|true|none|Timestamp of when the approval request was created|
|serviceKind|[ApprovalRequestServiceKind](#schemaapprovalrequestservicekind)|true|none|The approval service for this request. May be LaunchDarkly or an external approval service, such as ServiceNow or JIRA.|
|requestorId|string|false|none|The ID of the member who requested the approval|
|description|string|false|none|A human-friendly name for the approval request|
|reviewStatus|string|true|none|Current status of the review of this approval request|
|allReviews|[[ReviewResponse](#schemareviewresponse)]|true|none|An array of individual reviews of this approval request|
|notifyMemberIds|[string]|true|none|An array of member IDs. These members are notified to review the approval request.|
|notifyTeamKeys|[string]|false|none|An array of team keys, if teams were specified when the approval request was created. The members of these teams are listed in <code>notifyMemberIds</code>, resolved when the request was made. Team membership may have changed since then.|
|appliedDate|[UnixMillis](#schemaunixmillis)|false|none|Timestamp of when the approval request was applied|
|appliedByMemberId|string|false|none|The member ID of the member who applied the approval request|
|appliedByServiceTokenId|string|false|none|The service token ID of the service token which applied the approval request|
|status|string|true|none|Current status of the approval request|
|instructions|[Instructions](#schemainstructions)|true|none|List of instructions in semantic patch format to be applied to the feature flag|
|conflicts|[[Conflict](#schemaconflict)]|true|none|Details on any conflicting approval requests|
|_links|object|true|none|The location and content type of related resources|
|executionDate|[UnixMillis](#schemaunixmillis)|false|none|Timestamp for when instructions will be executed|
|operatingOnId|string|false|none|ID of scheduled change to edit or delete|
|integrationMetadata|[IntegrationMetadata](#schemaintegrationmetadata)|false|none|Details about the object in an external service corresponding to this approval request, such as a ServiceNow change request or a JIRA ticket, if an external approval service is being used|
|source|[CopiedFromEnv](#schemacopiedfromenv)|false|none|Details about the source feature flag, if copied|
|customWorkflowMetadata|[CustomWorkflowMeta](#schemacustomworkflowmeta)|false|none|Details about the custom workflow, if this approval request is part of a custom workflow|
|resourceId|string|false|none|String representation of a resource|
|approvalSettings|[ApprovalSettings](#schemaapprovalsettings)|false|none|The settings for this approval|
|project|[Project](#schemaproject)|false|none|Project the approval request belongs to|
|environments|[[Environment](#schemaenvironment)]|false|none|List of environments the approval impacts|
|flag|[ExpandedFlagRep](#schemaexpandedflagrep)|false|none|Flag the approval request belongs to|
|resource|[ExpandedResourceRep](#schemaexpandedresourcerep)|false|none|Resource the approval request belongs to|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|reviewStatus|approved|
|reviewStatus|declined|
|reviewStatus|pending|
|status|pending|
|status|completed|
|status|failed|
|status|scheduled|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|_id|string|false|none|The experiment ID|
|key|string|true|none|The experiment key|
|name|string|true|none|The experiment name|
|description|string|false|none|The experiment description|
|_maintainerId|string|true|none|The ID of the member who maintains this experiment.|
|_creationDate|[UnixMillis](#schemaunixmillis)|true|none|Timestamp of when the experiment was created|
|environmentKey|string|true|none|none|
|methodology|string|false|none|The results analysis approach.|
|dataSource|string|false|none|The source of metric data in order to analyze results. Defaults to "launchdarkly" when not provided.|
|archivedDate|[UnixMillis](#schemaunixmillis)|false|none|Timestamp of when the experiment was archived|
|tags|[string]|false|none|Tags for the experiment|
|_links|object|true|none|The location and content type of related resources|
|holdoutId|string|false|none|The holdout ID|
|currentIteration|[IterationRep](#schemaiterationrep)|false|none|Details on the current iteration|
|type|string|false|none|The experiment type|
|_access|[Access](#schemaaccess)|false|none|Details on the allowed and denied actions for this experiment|
|draftIteration|[IterationRep](#schemaiterationrep)|false|none|Details on the current iteration. This iteration may be already started, or may still be a draft.|
|previousIterations|[[IterationRep](#schemaiterationrep)]|false|none|Details on the previous iterations for this experiment.|
|analysisConfig|[AnalysisConfigRep](#schemaanalysisconfigrep)|false|none|Details of the Analysis Configuration for this experiment.|
|mutableFieldsByStatus|[MutableFieldsByStatusRep](#schemamutablefieldsbystatusrep)|false|none|Fields that can be changed for each iteration status.|

|customProperties|[CustomProperties](#schemacustomproperties)|false|none|Metadata attached to the feature flag, in the form of the property key associated with a name and array of values for the metadata to associate with this flag. Typically used to store data related to an integration.|
|defaults|[Defaults](#schemadefaults)|false|none|The indices, from the array of variations, for the variations to serve by default when targeting is on and when targeting is off. These variations will be used for this flag in new environments. If omitted, the first and last variation will be used.|

|maintainerId|string|false|none|The ID of the member who maintains this feature flag|
|maintainerTeamKey|string|false|none|The key of the team that maintains this feature flag|
|initialPrerequisites|[[FlagPrerequisitePost](#schemaflagprerequisitepost)]|false|none|Initial set of prerequisite flags for all environments|
|isFlagOn|boolean|false|none|Whether to automatically turn the flag on across all environments at creation. Defaults to <code>false</code>.|

```json
            "string"
          ]
        }
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|_id|string|true|none|none|
|status|string|true|none|none|
|description|string|false|none|none|
|holdoutAmount|string|true|none|The percentage of traffic allocated to this holdout.|
|isDirty|boolean|false|none|Indicates if the holdout experiment is running and if any related experiments are running.|
|createdAt|[UnixMillis](#schemaunixmillis)|true|none|none|
|updatedAt|[UnixMillis](#schemaunixmillis)|true|none|none|
|baseExperiment|[Experiment](#schemaexperiment)|true|none|none|
|relatedExperiments|[[Experiment](#schemaexperiment)]|false|none|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|status|created|
|status|enabled|
|status|running|
|status|ended|

<h2 id="tocS_HoldoutPatchInput">HoldoutPatchInput</h2>

<a id="tocsholdoutpatchinput"></a>

```json
{
  "comment": "Optional comment",
  "instructions": "[{\"kind\": \"updateName\", \"name\": \"Updated holdout name\"}]"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|comment|string|false|none|Optional comment describing the update|
|instructions|[Instructions](#schemainstructions)|true|none|The instructions to perform when updating. This should be an array with objects that look like <code>{"kind": "update_action"}</code>. Some instructions also require a <code>value</code> field in the array element.|

```json
{
  "name": "holdout-one-name",

  "description": "My holdout-one description",
  "randomizationunit": "user",
  "attributes": [
    "country",
    "device",
    "os"
  ],
  "holdoutamount": "10",
  "primarymetrickey": "metric-key-123abc",
  "metrics": [
    {
      "key": "metric-key-123abc",
      "isGroup": true,
      "primary": true,
      "analysisUnit": "user"
    }
  ],
  "prerequisiteflagkey": "flag-key-123abc",
  "maintainerId": "string"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|string|false|none|A human-friendly name for the holdout|
|key|string|false|none|A key that identifies the holdout|
|description|string|false|none|Description of the holdout|
|randomizationunit|string|false|none|The chosen randomization unit for the holdout base experiment|
|attributes|[string]|false|none|The attributes that the holdout iteration's results can be sliced by|
|holdoutamount|string|false|none|Audience allocation for the holdout|
|primarymetrickey|string|false|none|The key of the primary metric for this holdout|
|metrics|[[MetricInput](#schemametricinput)]|false|none|Details on the metrics for this experiment|
|prerequisiteflagkey|string|false|none|The key of the flag that the holdout is dependent on|
|maintainerId|string|false|none|Maintainer id|

|flags|[FlagsInput](#schemaflagsinput)|true|none|Details on the feature flag and targeting rules for this iteration|
|randomizationUnit|string|false|none|The unit of randomization for this iteration. Defaults to user.|
|reallocationFrequencyMillis|integer|false|none|The cadence (in milliseconds) to update the allocation.|
|covariateId|string|false|none|The ID of the covariate CSV|
|attributes|[string]|false|none|The attributes that this iteration's results can be sliced by|

|winningReason|string|false|none|The reason you stopped the experiment|
|canReshuffleTraffic|boolean|false|none|Whether the experiment may reassign traffic to different variations when the experiment audience changes (true) or must keep all traffic assigned to its initial variation (false).|
|flags|object|false|none|Details on the flag used in this experiment|
|reallocationFrequencyMillis|integer|false|none|The cadence (in milliseconds) to update the allocation. Only present for multi-armed bandits.|

|metrics|[[DependentMetricOrMetricGroupRep](#schemadependentmetricormetricgrouprep)]|false|none|Details on the metrics for this experiment|
|layerSnapshot|[LayerSnapshotRep](#schemalayersnapshotrep)|false|none|Snapshot of the layer state on iteration stop, if part of a layer. Otherwise omitted.|
|covariateInfo|[CovariateInfoRep](#schemacovariateinforep)|false|none|Details of the covariate file for stratified sampling|

|windowStartOffset|integer(int64)|false|none|Start of the measurement window in milliseconds|
|windowEndOffset|integer(int64)|false|none|End of the measurement window in milliseconds|
|winsorLowerPercentile|number|false|none|Lower winsorization percentile in the open interval (0, 100)|

|winsorIncludeImputed|boolean|false|none|When true, the percentile bound calculation includes imputed zeros|

|eventKey|string|false|none|The event key to use in your code. Required for custom conversion/binary and custom numeric metrics only.|
|successCriteria|string|false|none|Success criteria. Required for custom and trace numeric metrics, optional for custom and trace conversion metrics.|

|analysisType|string|false|none|The method for analyzing metric events|
|percentileValue|integer|false|none|The percentile for the analysis method. An integer denoting the target percentile between 0 and 100. Required when <code>analysisType</code> is <code>percentile</code>.|
|eventDefault|[MetricEventDefaultRep](#schemametriceventdefaultrep)|false|none|none|
|dataSource|[MetricDataSourceRefRep](#schemametricdatasourcerefrep)|false|none|none|
|filters|[EventFilter](#schemaeventfilter)|false|none|Filters for the metric to exclude certain events from being included. This is only supported for custom metrics.|
|windowStartOffset|integer(int64)|false|none|Not yet implemented - The start of the measurement window, in milliseconds relative to the unit's first exposure to a flag variation|
|windowEndOffset|integer(int64)|false|none|Not yet implemented - The end of the measurement window, in milliseconds relative to the unit's first exposure to a flag variation|
|winsorLowerPercentile|number|false|none|Lower winsorization percentile, expressed as a percent in the open interval (0, 100). When both bounds are set, defines a two-sided clamp range. Otherwise lower-only winsorization.|
|winsorUpperPercentile|number|false|none|Upper winsorization percentile, expressed as a percent in the open interval (0, 100). When both bounds are set, must be greater than winsorLowerPercentile.|
|winsorIncludeImputed|boolean|false|none|When true, the percentile bound calculation includes imputed zeros. Only meaningful when at least one bound is set and the metric includes units that didn't send events.|
|traceQuery|string|false|none|The trace query to use for the metric. Required for trace metrics.|
|traceValueLocation|string|false|none|The location in the trace to use for numeric values. Required for numeric trace metrics.|
|unitAggregationField|string|false|none|The warehouse column to use for counting distinct values. Required when the unitAggregationType is count_distinct.|
|valueColumn|string|false|none|For numeric warehouse-native metrics, the column holding the numeric value. Overrides the value column mapped on the data source.|
|denominator|[DenominatorPost](#schemadenominatorpost)|false|none|For ratio metrics, the denominator event configuration. Only supported for warehouse native custom metrics.|

```json
      "op": "string",
      "values": [
        null

      "negate": true

  ],

  "description": "string",
  "ref": "string"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|_id|string|false|none|The flag rule ID|
|disabled|boolean|false|none|Whether the rule is disabled|
|variation|integer|false|none|The index of the variation, from the array of variations for this flag|
|rollout|[Rollout](#schemarollout)|false|none|Details on the percentage rollout, if it exists|
|clauses|[[Clause](#schemaclause)]|true|none|An array of clauses used for individual targeting based on attributes|
|trackEvents|boolean|true|none|Whether the SDK sends a detailed event for every evaluation of this rule, instead of only summary counts. Required for Data Export, but doesn't enable Data Export on its own.|
|description|string|false|none|The rule description|
|ref|string|false|none|none|

|excluded|[string]|false|none|An array of keys for excluded targets. Segment rules bypass individual excluded targets, so they will never be included based on rules. Excluded targets may still be included explicitly. This value is omitted for list-based segments over 15,000 entries, also called big segments.|

|unbounded|boolean|false|none|Whether this is a standard segment (<code>false</code>) or a big segment (<code>true</code>). Standard segments include rule-based segments and smaller list-based segments. Big segments include larger list-based segments and synced segments. If omitted, the segment is a standard segment.|
|unboundedContextKind|string|false|none|For big segments, the targeted context kind.|
|generation|integer|true|none|For big segments, how many times this segment has been created.|
|_unboundedMetadata|[SegmentMetadata](#schemasegmentmetadata)|false|none|Details on the external data store backing this segment. Only applies to big segments.|
|_external|string|false|none|The external data store backing this segment. Only applies to synced segments.|
|_externalLink|string|false|none|The URL for the external data store backing this segment. Only applies to synced segments.|
|_importInProgress|boolean|false|none|Whether an import is currently in progress for the specified segment. Only applies to big segments.|

Use this for a judge that scores bad output, such as a toxicity or hallucination judge.<br>- `false`: A higher score is better. Use this for a judge that scores good output, such as an accuracy or relevance judge.<br><br>The response includes this field only when `mode` is `judge`. For a built-in judge key, the value is always the built-in direction. Built-in judge keys are `ld-ai-judge-accuracy`, `ld-ai-judge-relevance`, and `ld-ai-judge-toxicity`, with or without a `-<timestamp>` suffix such as `ld-ai-judge-accuracy-1760000000000`. A custom judge with no stored direction omits this field.<br>|
