### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|description|string|false|none|A description of the AI Config|
|key|string|true|none|A unique key for the AI Config|
|maintainerId|string|false|none|The ID of the member who maintains this resource|
|maintainerTeamKey|string|false|none|The key of the team that maintains this resource|
|mode|string|false|none|The AI Config mode|
|name|string|true|none|A human-readable name for the AI Config|
|tags|[string]|false|none|Tags for this resource|
|viewKeys|[string]|false|none|Keys of the views to add the AI Config to|
|defaultVariation|[AIConfigVariationPost](#schemaaiconfigvariationpost)|false|none|none|
|evaluationMetricKey|string|false|none|Evaluation metric key for this config|
|isInverted|boolean|false|none|The success direction of a judge. Offline evaluations use it to decide whether a score passes.<br><br>- `true`: A lower score is better. Use this for a judge that scores bad output, such as a toxicity or hallucination judge.<br>- `false`: A higher score is better. Use this for a judge that scores good output, such as an accuracy or relevance judge.<br><br>**Required for a custom judge.** A custom judge has `mode` set to `judge` and a `key` that is not a built-in judge key. Built-in judge keys are `ld-ai-judge-accuracy`, `ld-ai-judge-relevance`, and `ld-ai-judge-toxicity`, with or without a `-<timestamp>` suffix such as `ld-ai-judge-accuracy-1760000000000`. For a built-in judge key, this field is optional, and the API always uses the built-in direction.<br><br>Do not send this field when `mode` is `agent` or `completion`.<br><br>This field is not in the schema's `required` list, because only custom judges need it.<br><br>The API returns a `400` error in these cases:<br>- `isInverted is required for a custom judge: ...`: You create a custom judge without this field. Send `true` or `false`.<br>- `isInverted is only supported for judge mode`: You send this field and `mode` is `agent` or `completion`. Remove the field, or set `mode` to `judge`.<br>- `isInverted is not supported`: Custom judges are not available for your account. Remove the field from the request.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|mode|agent|
|mode|completion|
|mode|judge|

Use this for a judge that scores bad output, such as a toxicity or hallucination judge.<br>- `false`: A higher score is better. Use this for a judge that scores good output, such as an accuracy or relevance judge.<br><br>Send this field only when the AI Config's `mode` is `judge`. If you omit it, the current direction does not change. For a built-in judge key, the API always returns the built-in direction. Built-in judge keys are `ld-ai-judge-accuracy`, `ld-ai-judge-relevance`, and `ld-ai-judge-toxicity`, with or without a `-<timestamp>` suffix such as `ld-ai-judge-accuracy-1760000000000`.<br><br>The API returns a `400` error in these cases:<br>- `isInverted is only supported for judge mode`: You send this field and the AI Config's `mode` is `agent` or `completion`. ### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|classifiers|[[Classifier](#schemaclassifier)]|false|none|Replaces classifier rules on a judge variation. An empty array clears them. When this array is<br>non-empty, messages must be empty.<br>|
|comment|string|false|none|Human-readable description of what this patch changes|
|description|string|false|none|Description for agent when the config is in agent mode.|
|instructions|string|false|none|Instructions for agent when the config is in agent mode.|
|messages|[[Message](#schemamessage)]|false|none|The prompt messages for this variation|
|model|object|false|none|Freeform JSON object. LaunchDarkly does not validate the keys. In a model config, `params` and `customParams` hold parameters that the provider's API accepts, for example `{"temperature": 0.7, "maxTokens": 4096}`.|
|modelConfigKey|string|false|none|The key that GET /api/v2/projects/{projectKey}/ai-configs/model-configs returns for the<br>model config. Do not use a custom model config's ID, which is the provider model ID.<br>|
|modelConfigVersion|integer|false|none|The exact model config version to set this variation to. Requires modelConfigKey to be<br>set (either in this patch or already on the variation), and the version must exist for<br>that model config. When omitted, the variation keeps the version it is currently set to,<br>unless the patch changes modelConfigKey, in which case the variation records the new<br>model config's current (latest) version.<br>|
|name|string|false|none|A human-readable name for the variation|
|outputFormat|object|false|none|JSON Schema defining the structured output format for the variation.|
|published|boolean|false|none|Whether to publish this version of the variation|
|state|string|false|none|The state to move the variation to. Omit this field to keep the current state.<br>- `archived`: Archive a published variation. You cannot archive a variation that is already archived. You also cannot archive the only variation of an AI Config. An AI Config itself cannot be archived.<br>- `published`: Restore an archived variation. You cannot publish a variation that is already published.<br>|
|tools|[[VariationToolPost](#schemavariationtoolpost)]|false|none|List of tools to use for this variation. The latest version of the tool will be used.|
|toolKeys|[string]|false|none|List of tool keys to use for this variation. The latest version of the tool will be used.|
|skills|[[VariationSkillPost](#schemavariationskillpost)]|false|none|List of agent skills to attach to this variation. Replaces the current attachments.|
|judgeConfiguration|[JudgeConfiguration](#schemajudgeconfiguration)|false|none|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|state|archived|
|state|published|

|maintainerId|string|false|none|The member ID of the maintainer. Not applied on create. To set the maintainer, update the model config after you create it.|
|maintainerTeamKey|string|false|none|The key of the team that maintains the model config. Not applied on create. To set the maintainer, update the model config after you create it.|
|icon|string|false|none|Icon for the model|
|provider|string|false|none|Provider for the model. Use the provider prefix of `key`. Cannot be changed after creation.|
|params|object|false|none|Freeform JSON object. LaunchDarkly does not validate the keys. In a model config, `params` and `customParams` hold parameters that the provider's API accepts, for example `{"temperature": 0.7, "maxTokens": 4096}`.|
|customParams|object|false|none|Freeform JSON object. LaunchDarkly does not validate the keys. In a model config, `params` and `customParams` hold parameters that the provider's API accepts, for example `{"temperature": 0.7, "maxTokens": 4096}`.|
|tags|[string]|false|none|Tags for the model config|
|costPerInputToken|number(double)|false|none|Cost per input token in USD|
|costPerOutputToken|number(double)|false|none|Cost per output token in USD|
|costPerCachedInputToken|number(double)|false|none|Cost per cached input token in USD|

<h2 id="tocS_ModelConfigPatch">ModelConfigPatch</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemamodelconfigpatch"></a>
<a id="schema_ModelConfigPatch"></a>
<a id="tocSmodelconfigpatch"></a>
<a id="tocsmodelconfigpatch"></a>

```json
{
  "costPerOutputToken": 0.00004,
  "maintainerId": "507f1f77bcf86cd799439011",
  "costPerInputToken": 0.000005,
  "provider": "provider",
  "customParams": "{}",
  "name": "GPT Image 2",
  "maintainerTeamKey": "example-team-key",
  "id": "id",
  "params": "{}",
  "costPerCachedInputToken": 0.00000125,
  "tags": [
    "image"
  ]
}
```

Fields to update. Omitted fields keep their current values. `params`, `customParams`, and `tags` replace the current values. Global model configs cannot be updated.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string|false|none|Immutable provider model identifier. To use a different model identifier, create a new model config.|
|provider|string|false|none|Immutable model provider. To use a different provider, create a new model config.|
|name|string|false|none|Human-readable name of the model|
|costPerInputToken|number(double)|false|none|Cost per input token in USD|
|costPerOutputToken|number(double)|false|none|Cost per output token in USD|
|costPerCachedInputToken|number(double)|false|none|Cost per cached input token in USD|
|params|object|false|none|Freeform JSON object. LaunchDarkly does not validate the keys. In a model config, `params` and `customParams` hold parameters that the provider's API accepts, for example `{"temperature": 0.7, "maxTokens": 4096}`.|
|customParams|object|false|none|Freeform JSON object. LaunchDarkly does not validate the keys. In a model config, `params` and `customParams` hold parameters that the provider's API accepts, for example `{"temperature": 0.7, "maxTokens": 4096}`.|
|tags|[string]|false|none|Tags for the model config. Replaces the current tags.|
|maintainerId|string|false|none|The member ID of the new maintainer. Set `maintainerId` or `maintainerTeamKey`, not both. An empty string removes the maintainer.|
|maintainerTeamKey|string|false|none|The key of the team to set as the new maintainer. Set `maintainerId` or `maintainerTeamKey`, not both.|

<h2 id="tocS_RestrictedModelError">RestrictedModelError</h2>

<a id="schemarestrictedmodelerror"></a>

<a id="tocSrestrictedmodelerror"></a>
<a id="tocsrestrictedmodelerror"></a>

```json
{
  "code": 400,
  "message": "key is already in use",
  "key": "OpenAI.gpt-image-2"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|key|string|true|none|The model config key that was not added|
|message|string|true|none|Why the key was not added. A key that a config variation uses cannot be restricted. Move those variations to a different model first.|
|code|integer|true|none|HTTP status code for this key. `400` means a config variation uses the key. `404` means the key does not exist in the project.|

Request body for updating an agent graph. If rootConfigKey or edges are present, both must be present.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|string|false|none|A human-readable name for the agent graph|
|description|string|false|none|A description of the agent graph|
|maintainerId|string|false|none|The ID of the member who maintains this agent graph. Pass an empty string to remove maintainer.|
|maintainerTeamKey|string|false|none|The key of the team that maintains this agent graph. Pass an empty string to remove maintainer.|
|rootConfigKey|string|false|none|The config key of the root node. If present, edges must also be present.|
|edges|[[AgentGraphEdge](#schemaagentgraphedge)]|false|none|The edges in the graph. If present, rootConfigKey must also be present. Replaces all existing edges.|

A usage of an AI tool in a specific AgentControl config variation.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|aiConfigKey|string|true|none|The key of the AgentControl config with a variation that references this tool.|

|variationId|string|true|none|The ID of the variation that references this tool.|
|variationKey|string|true|none|The key of the AgentControl config variation that references this tool.|
|variationName|string|true|none|The name of the variation that references this tool.|
|toolVersion|integer|true|none|The version of the tool being referenced.|

|description|string|false|none|Description of the metric|
|category|string|false|none|The category of the metric|

|successCriteria|string|false|none|For custom and trace metrics, the success criteria|
|unit|string|false|none|For numeric custom and trace metrics, the unit of measure|
|eventKey|string|false|none|For custom metrics, the event key to use in your code|
|randomizationUnits|[string]|false|none|**Deprecated.** Deprecated, use <code>analysisUnits</code> instead.|
|analysisUnits|[string]|false|none|An array of analysis units allowed for this metric.|
|filters|[AiConfigsFilter](#schemaaiconfigsfilter)|false|none|none|
|unitAggregationType|string|false|none|The method by which multiple unit event values are aggregated|
|analysisType|string|false|none|The method for analyzing metric events|
|percentileValue|integer|false|none|The percentile for the analysis method. An integer denoting the target percentile between 0 and 100. Required when <code>analysisType</code> is <code>percentile</code>.|
|eventDefault|[AiConfigsMetricEventDefaultRep](#schemaaiconfigsmetriceventdefaultrep)|false|none|none|

|selector|string|false|none|For click metrics, the CSS selectors|
|urls|[[UrlMatcher](#schemaurlmatcher)]|false|none|none|
|windowStartOffset|integer(int64)|false|none|Not yet implemented - The start of the measurement window, in milliseconds relative to the unit's first exposure to a flag variation|
|windowEndOffset|integer(int64)|false|none|Not yet implemented - The end of the measurement window, in milliseconds relative to the unit's first exposure to a flag variation|
|winsorLowerPercentile|number|false|none|Lower winsorization percentile, expressed as a percent in the open interval (0, 100). When both bounds are set, defines a two-sided clamp range. Otherwise lower-only winsorization.|
|winsorUpperPercentile|number|false|none|Upper winsorization percentile, expressed as a percent in the open interval (0, 100). When both bounds are set, must be greater than winsorLowerPercentile.|
|winsorIncludeImputed|boolean|false|none|When true, the percentile bound calculation includes imputed zeros. Only meaningful when at least one bound is set and the metric includes units that didn't send events.|
|traceQuery|string|false|none|For trace metrics, the trace query to use for the metric.|
|traceValueLocation|string|false|none|For trace metrics, the location in the trace to use for numeric values.|
|unitAggregationField|string|false|none|For count_distinct metrics, the column to count distinct values of|

  "autoApplyApprovedChanges": true,
  "serviceKind": "launchdarkly",
  "serviceConfig": {},

    "require-approval"
  ],
  "serviceKindConfigurationId": "1ef45a85-218f-4428-a8b2-a97e5f56c258"
}
```

Configuration that controls how changes to a resource are gated by approvals.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|required|boolean|true|none|If approvals are required for this environment|
|bypassApprovalsForPendingChanges|boolean|true|none|Whether to skip approvals for pending changes|
|minNumApprovals|integer(int)|true|none|Sets the amount of approvals required before a member can apply a change. The minimum is one and the maximum is five.<br>|
|canReviewOwnRequest|boolean|true|none|Allow someone who makes an approval request to apply their own change|
|canApplyDeclinedChanges|boolean|true|none|Allow applying the change as long as at least one person has approved|
|autoApplyApprovedChanges|boolean \| null|false|none|Automatically apply changes that have been approved by all reviewers. This field is only applicable for approval services other than LaunchDarkly.<br>|
|serviceKind|string|true|none|Which service to use for managing approvals|
|serviceConfig|object|true|none|Arbitrary service-specific configuration|
|requiredApprovalTags|[string]|true|none|Require approval only on flags with the provided tags. Otherwise all flags will require approval.<br>|
|serviceKindConfigurationId|string \| null|false|none|Optional integration configuration ID of a custom approval integration. This is an Enterprise-only feature.<br>|

|filter|string|false|none|Optional filter string to determine which resources should be linked. Resources only need to match either the filter or explicitly-listed keys to be linked (union).<br>Uses the same syntax as list endpoints: flags use comma-separated field:value filters, segments use queryfilter syntax.<br><br>Supported filters by resource type:<br>- flags: query, tags, maintainerId, maintainerTeamKey, type, status, state, staleState, sdkAvailability, targeting, hasExperiment, hasDataExport, evaluated, creationDate, contextKindTargeted, contextKindsEvaluated, filterEnv, segmentTargeted, codeReferences.min, codeReferences.max, excludeSettings, releasePipeline, applicationEvaluated, purpose, guardedRollout, view, key, name, archived, followerId<br>- segments (queryfilter): query, tags, keys, excludedKeys, unbounded, external, view, type<br>Some filters are only available when the corresponding feature is enabled on your account.<br>|
|comment|string|false|none|Optional comment for the link/unlink operation|

Resources only need to match either the filter or explicitly-listed keys to be linked (union).<br>Uses the same queryfilter syntax as the segments list endpoint.<br><br>Supported filters for segments: query, tags, keys, excludedKeys, unbounded, external, view, type<br>|

|comment|string|false|none|Optional comment for the link/unlink operation|

Uses the same syntax as list endpoints: flags use comma-separated field:value filters, segments use queryfilter syntax.<br><br>Supported filters by resource type:<br>- flags: query, tags, maintainerId, maintainerTeamKey, type, status, state, staleState, sdkAvailability, targeting, hasExperiment, hasDataExport, evaluated, creationDate, contextKindTargeted, contextKindsEvaluated, filterEnv, segmentTargeted, codeReferences.min, codeReferences.max, excludeSettings, releasePipeline, applicationEvaluated, purpose, guardedRollout, view, key, name, archived, followerId<br>- segments (queryfilter): query, tags, keys, excludedKeys, unbounded, external, view, type<br>Some filters are only available when the corresponding feature is enabled on your account.<br>|
|environmentId|string|false|none|Required when using filter for segment resources. Specifies which environment to query for segments matching the filter.<br>Ignored for flag resources (flags are global across environments).<br>|
|comment|string|false|none|Optional comment for the link/unlink operation|

<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemareleasetype"></a>

```

Whether the release uses metric monitoring.

<h2 id="tocS_ReleaseStatus">ReleaseStatus</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemareleasestatus"></a>
<a id="schema_ReleaseStatus"></a>
<a id="tocSreleasestatus"></a>
<a id="tocsreleasestatus"></a>

```json
"pending"
```

High-level status of an environment release or release phase.
- `pending`: The release or phase has not started.
- `in_progress`: The release or phase is progressing without requiring action.
- `waiting`: The release is partially rolled out, but is paused and waiting for action from the user.
- `completed`: The release or phase reached the target variation.
- `reverted`: The release or phase returned to the original variation.

<h2 id="tocS_ReleaseStatusReason">ReleaseStatusReason</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemareleasestatusreason"></a>
<a id="schema_ReleaseStatusReason"></a>
<a id="tocSreleasestatusreason"></a>
<a id="tocsreleasestatusreason"></a>

```json
"waiting_regression_detected"
```

Additional detail for a `waiting`, `completed`, or `reverted` status.
The field may be absent for a `waiting` status when there is no
specific reason.
`waiting_phase_ended` appears only on the release, never on a phase.
It means a phase of a multi-phase release with `advancementMode`
`manual` ended and the release must be advanced to the next phase.
`reverted_discarded` means the phase ended without a regression or a
member rolling it back. A running phase is discarded when the flag
changes underneath it, for example when the flag is turned off,
archived, or deleted. A pending phase is discarded when the release
ends before it starts, either because an earlier phase reverted or
because the release was stopped with a resolution that removes pending
phases. A release reports `reverted_discarded` only when the last phase
that started was discarded.

<h2 id="tocS_CleanupBehavior">CleanupBehavior</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemacleanupbehavior"></a>
<a id="schema_CleanupBehavior"></a>
<a id="tocScleanupbehavior"></a>
<a id="tocscleanupbehavior"></a>

```json
"remove_rules_and_update_default_rule"
```

What happens to the release rules when the final phase completes,
either on its own or because a stop rolls it forward while it's
running:

- `remove_rules_and_update_default_rule`: The release rules are
  removed and the default rule serves the target variation.
- `leave_rules_in_place`: The release rules stay and serve the
  target variation.

In every other case, including a revert, it has no effect: release
rules left on the flag keep serving the variation the release ended
on, ahead of rules added later without `beforeRuleId`.

<h2 id="tocS_EnvironmentReleaseResolution">EnvironmentReleaseResolution</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaenvironmentreleaseresolution"></a>
<a id="schema_EnvironmentReleaseResolution"></a>
<a id="tocSenvironmentreleaseresolution"></a>
<a id="tocsenvironmentreleaseresolution"></a>

```json
"roll_forward_all_phases"
```

How to resolve each phase of the release when you stop it:

- `roll_forward_all_phases`: All phases serve the target variation.
  Pending phases stay on the flag and are enabled.
- `roll_forward_current_phase_and_remove_pending_phases`: Current and
  completed phases serve the target variation. Pending phases are
  removed.
- `roll_back_all_phases_and_remove_pending_phases`: Current and
  completed phases serve the original variation. Pending phases are
  removed.
- `roll_back_current_phase_and_remove_pending_phases`: The current
  phase serves the original variation, and completed phases keep
  serving the target variation. Pending phases are removed.

For a single-phase release there are no completed or pending phases,
so the two roll-forward values are equivalent, as are the two roll-back
values.

The `current_phase` values return `400` if the release is between
phases. Use an `all_phases` value instead. A terminal release returns
`200` unchanged for every resolution.

Pending phases are<br>  removed.<br>- `roll_back_all_phases_and_remove_pending_phases`: Current and<br>  completed phases serve the original variation. Pending phases are<br>  removed.<br>- `roll_back_current_phase_and_remove_pending_phases`: The current<br>  phase serves the original variation, and completed phases keep<br>  serving the target variation. Pending phases are removed.<br><br>For a single-phase release there are no completed or pending phases,<br>so the two roll-forward values are equivalent, as are the two roll-back<br>values.<br><br>The `current_phase` values return `400` if the release is between<br>phases. Use an `all_phases` value instead. A terminal release returns<br>`200` unchanged for every resolution.<br>|
|comment|string|false|none|Optional comment written to the flag's audit-log entry.|

|resolution|roll_back_current_phase_and_remove_pending_phases|
